title: Hurricane Isaias rapidly intensifies as evacuation orders expand to several cities
description: THE...
fullText:
Hurricane Isaias is continuing to strengthen in the Gulf after becoming the first Atlantic hurricane of the season and expected to make landfall along the northern Gulf Coast later this week as a dangerous Category 2 hurricane.

Isaias is expected to approach the coast by Friday, with landfall currently estimated to be sometime late Friday or early Saturday between Gulf Shores, Alabama, and Pensacola, Florida.

Isaias strengthened from a Category 1 to a Category 2 hurricane on Thursday, with sustained winds of 100 mph as it moves northeast at 12 mph.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey and Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp have declared states of emergency ahead of the storm.

In a Thursday press conference, DeSantis urged residents to prepare now, including filling up their gas tanks and stocking up on enough water and nonperishable food to last through a potential power outage.

"If you are in the Panhandle, assume that you are going to lose power," DeSantis said. "Prepare to lose power. That is likely to happen with a storm that is at hurricane status."

Over a dozen Florida and Alabama counties have canceled school through the end of the week, and multiple colleges have closed their campuses.

Meanwhile, evacuation orders have been issued for Dauphin Island in Alabama, as well as Okaloosa and Escambia counties in Florida.

Mandatory evacuation orders have also been issued in Walton County, Florida.

The Alabama beach towns of Gulf Shores and Orange Beach released a joint statement urging voluntary evacuations ahead of Isaias' arrival.

"In anticipation of the expected impacts from Tropical Storm Isaias, the cities of Gulf Shores and Orange Beach are encouraging all non‑residents, and residents living in low-lying, flood prone areas to voluntarily evacuate," the statement said. "City officials urge all individuals who are not permanent residents to leave the area immediately and relocate to a safer location."

Both Shell and Chevron have instituted shut-in production procedures across five of their offshore oil facilities in the Gulf and removed non-essential workers, respectively.

BP said it was also removing non-essential personnel and securing offshore facilities. ExxonMobil operations are currently normal, but they are monitoring the forecast closely.

HURRICANE ISAIAS CHURNS IN GULF AS OIL RIGS PREPARE FOR POTENTIALLY DANGEROUS CONDITIONS

Hurricane Isaias strengthened from Tropical Storm Isaias late Wednesday night.

In their Wednesday 11 p.m. update, the National Hurricane Center kept Isaias at tropical storm strength. About 30 minutes later, they released a special advisory stating that Isaias had indeed strengthened into a Category 1 hurricane.

WHAT’S THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A TROPICAL DEPRESSION, TROPICAL STORM AND HURRICANE?

Isaias rapidly intensified from a tropical storm into a Category 1 hurricane, with winds increasing by 40 mph in just 6 hours between Wednesday afternoon and late Wednesday night.

Isaias' forecast cone shows it heading directly toward the northern Gulf Coast, with impacts centered over roughly 30 million people in Louisiana, Alabama, Mississippi and the Florida Panhandle.

Tropical weather advisories have expanded inland, across parts of southern Alabama and southwestern Georgia.

A Hurricane Warning is in effect from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to the Bay/Gulf County Line in Florida.

LATEST FROM FOX WEATHER HURRICANE SPECIALIST BRYAN NORCROSS

A Storm Surge Warning is also in effect from the mouth of the Mississippi to the Suwannee River in Florida's Big Bend region.

"The combination of a dangerous storm surge and the tide will cause normally dry areas near the coast to be flooded by rising waters moving inland from the shoreline," the NHC said.

Currently, between 5 and 7 feet of surge is forecast for Mobile Bay and from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to Indian Pass, Florida.

Heavy rain is expected to begin on Friday, with flash flooding, damaging wind gusts, storm surge and even tornadoes possible as the storm comes ashore.

Hurricane Hunters are continuing to conduct regular reconnaissance missions into Hurricane Isaias to collect the latest forecast data.

"The eye of Isaias has become apparent on visible and infrared satellite imagery," the NHC said. "Interestingly, this is the first eye noted on satellite pictures in the Atlantic basin during the 2026 Hurricane Season."

FOX WEATHER JOINS THE HURRICANE HUNTERS ON CRITICAL RECON MISSION INTO TROPICAL STORM ISAIAS

The storm is expected to continue to strengthen early Friday, with heavy rain reaching parts of the Gulf Coast as early as Friday morning.

"Residents from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle should closely monitor the latest forecast updates and ensure they have their hurricane plan in place," the NHC said.

FOX Weather Hurricane Specialist Bryan Norcross noted that several dynamic factors still remain at play, which will determine how strong and exactly where Isaias will make landfall, namely the storm's angle of approach and how the winds will impact the storm as it comes ashore.

TIMELINE: WHERE TROPICAL STORM ISAIAS IS HEADED AND WHEN IT COULD BECOME A HURRICANE

Some forecast models show Isaias weakening at landfall, while others show the storm strengthening as strong winds high in the atmosphere interact with it from the north.

Norcross said most of the storm's most impactful weather will most likely be on the right side of the storm's center.

Meanwhile, NOAA's Weather Prediction Center (WPC) has issued a flash flood risk for Friday across portions of Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Florida, Georgia, as well as southern portions of Tennessee, southwestern North Carolina and western South Carolina.

A Level 3 out of 4 flash flood risk covers Mobile, Alabama, and the Florida Panhandle west of Panama City. A Level 2 risk includes Atlanta and Montgomery, Alabama, and eventually shifts inland into Saturday to include the Carolinas and Tennessee Valley.

7 FACTS YOU SHOULD KNOW ABOUT FLASH FLOODS

"Rainfall estimates currently show 6 to 10 inches with localized higher amounts which will lead to flash and urban flooding and eventually river flooding," the FOX Forecast Center said.

NOAA's Storm Prediction Center (SPC) has issued a Level 2 out of 5 risk of severe weather for Saturday across southern Alabama and into the Florida Panhandle, with a particular threat of tornadoes as the storm's outer bands come ashore.

TROPICAL STORM ISAIAS CHURNS IN GULF AS OIL RIGS PREPARE FOR POTENTIALLY DANGEROUS CONDITIONS

The system is expected to move inland quickly with heavy rain spreading across the Southeast Saturday, triggering a broad Level 2 flash flood risk from some places along the Mississippi River to the Southeast coast.

This story is developing. Check back frequently for updates.

title: Your Mac Should Be Doing More of the Work. Here's How MacPaw Helps
description: Setapp, CleanMyMac, and Eney take everyday Mac work off your hands without adding one more thing to manage.
fullText:
The work you actually sat down to do rarely gets interrupted by something dramatic. It gets interrupted by housekeeping—a quick fix here, a quick lookup there, each one small enough to feel harmless and just long enough to break your focus.

This is true for freelancers, founders, designers, and developers. But it’s also true for work-from-home employees and busy people in general. And it’s not that any of these tasks are difficult (which almost makes them more annoying); it’s that each one takes just enough time and attention to pull you away from whatever you actually sat down to do. Little interruptions may not seem like much, but they add up to a surprising amount of time spent taking care of your Mac instead of letting your Mac take care of you.

MacPaw has spent 18 years building tools that take everyday work off Mac users' hands by noticing the small stuff you've stopped noticing, and quietly handling it for you. For anyone whose Mac doubles as an office, the files, apps, and projects add up—but the upkeep shouldn't have to.

Here’s how MacPaw’s products help you save time and frustration while using your trusty Mac computer.

When storage starts disappearing, you can open folders one by one, sort through old downloads, track down duplicate files, and try to uncover large files that are eating up space and collecting dust. Or, you can make that maintenance somebody else's problem.

CleanMyMac keeps everyday care in one place, so maintenance takes less of your attention. If you work with video or like to keep many applications open at once, freeing up space can help your Mac work as intended. You’ll spend less time staring at the dreaded spinning color wheel and more time getting things done.

Sometimes you just need an app for one specific task. Maybe you need to compress a video before sending it to a client. The job itself takes two minutes, but first you have to find an app, compare your options, figure out whether you trust it, download it, and possibly even pay for yet another subscription.

Setapp cuts out much of the scavenger hunt by giving you one trusted place to look for the right app, so a two-minute task doesn't start with 15 minutes of searching, comparing, and managing software. It also makes it easy to discover time-savers and cool tricks you didn't even realize were possible on a Mac.

Splitting a PDF or trimming the first few seconds from a video isn't complicated, but if you only do it occasionally, you might still end up digging through menus or Googling it all over again. title: We Now Know When Apple Will Host Its Next Big Tech Event
description: Apple's next event is titled "Welcome Home."
fullText:
Last month's Apple event was a big one. The company announced (and subsequently released) the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, Apple Watch Series 12, and Apple Watch Ultra 4. It also announced the iPhone Duo, though the company's first foldable phone still isn't out yet. Despite all these new products, Apple apparently wasn't finished. Next week, the company will host another product announcement, titled "Welcome Home." Here's what we know.

Apple's product announcement hints are usually pretty subtle. This time, it isn't. "Welcome Home" is almost assuredly referencing Apple's long-rumored smart home devices. Sure, the company makes some smart devices, like the HomePod and HomePod mini, but leaks suggest the company has some big updates up its sleeve.

Perhaps no announcement will be bigger than its smart home hub. This device, according to the rumor mill, will be a mix between an iPad and a HomePod, competing with similar devices from companies like Amazon and Google. It may ship with a six-inch display (some reports suggest the screen is a square), but it won't be like an iPad on a stand. Instead, the experience seems more focused, letting you control smart home devices, make and receive FaceTime calls, watch videos, display the news and water data, and check your calendar. Of course, it will likely work with Siri AI, the company's new AI-powered assistant.

Apple may even expect users to buy more than one of these hubs. The idea could be to have multiple hubs throughout your house, which could let you use them like intercoms. (Apple currently offers a similar feature with its HomePods.) If the rumors are to be believed, the smart hub will understand the voice of whoever is talking to it, and tailor the experience to that user personally. If you have guests over, you could switch to a "visitor mode" to avoid revealing sensitive information.

While the smart home hub may steal the show, Apple is planning some updates to existing devices as well. The HomePod mini may come in new colors, and is expected to get both the N1 chip for improvements to wifi and Bluetooth, as well as an upgraded S-series chip for Siri AI. Apple may also update the Apple TV 4K with the A19 or A19 Pro chip, as well as that new N1 chip, and a new Siri remote. Apple may take this opportunity to reveal its new OLED iPad mini, but the company may keep the focus on smart home specifically.

According to Apple's announcement, "Welcome Home" kicks off on Tuesday, Oct. 13 at 9 a.m. ET (6 a.m. PT). That's an early start time, considering the company is based in California, though it seems Apple is hosting the event in New York City this time around. For context, Apple's events usually kick off at 1 p.m. ET (10 a.m. PT) when the company hosts them in Cupertino. It's not yet clear if there will be a livestream of the event, or if it will be exclusive for invited members of the media.

title: Celtic Challenge introduces home final incentive
description: Irish, Scottish and Welsh teams have the added incentive of competing for a home final in the 2026-27 Celtic Challenge.
fullText:
The final of the 2026-27 Celtic Challenge will be played at the ground of the highest-ranked team rather than a neutral venue.

The cross-border competition, which features two clubs from each of Ireland, Scotland and Wales, gets under way on Saturday, 5 December.

Teams play five home and away fixtures in the regular season and there is an added incentive for placings, with the higher seed of the two semi-final winners hosting the final.

Last season Wolfhounds beat Irish rivals Clovers in a final played at Hive Stadium in Edinburgh.

The champions, who won the title for the third successive season, get the 2026-27 campaign under way at home to Welsh side Brython Thunder in Belfast.

Edinburgh also travel to Ireland to face Clovers while the other Welsh team, Gwalia Lightning, entertain Glasgow.

title: Everton's Sherif fined for breaching betting rules
description: The Football Association fines Everton forward Martin Sherif £5,000 for breaching its betting rules over a 15-month period.
fullText:
Everton forward Martin Sherif has been fined £5,000 by the Football Association for breaching its betting rules over a 15-month period.

The 20-year-old admitted having caused, permitted or enabled 61 bets on games between 20 November 2024 and 12 February 2026.

In his defence, Sherif said he did not place any of the bets himself but admitted they came from accounts in his name and which he funded.

An independent regulatory commission said Sherif had shown "genuine remorse".

The striker, who was born in Liberia and is a Netherlands youth international, joined Everton's youth set-up in 2019 and began training with the first team in early 2025.

In February he joined Port Vale on loan for the remainder of the season, scoring twice in 17 League One appearances as they were relegated.

title: Wales target clean sheet in World Cup play-off first leg
description: Rhian Wilkinson makes a clean sheet the first target for Wales in Friday's Women's World Cup play-off semi-final first leg against Albania.
fullText:
Rhian Wilkinson has identified a clean sheet as the first target for Wales in Friday's Women's World Cup play-off semi-final first leg against Albania.

Wales face Albania at the 16,000-capacity Loro Borici Stadium in Shkoder before next Tuesday's return in Llanelli.

Wilkinson's side beat their play-off opponents twice during the group stage of World Cup qualifying in April, when they followed up a 4-0 home victory with a scrappy 1-0 success on their travels.

Wales have not been helped by a string of injuries as they prepare for another double-header against Albania.

When asked what would represent a positive first leg for Wales, Wilkinson said: "I'll stick with a clean sheet and a strong performance."

She added: "I think what I would say is that this is home and away, back-to-back play-off and we've had some experiences with this.

"We continue to grow through those and it's about taking care of delivering a performance away and then making sure we come home and deliver another one in the next few days."

Women's World Cup qualifying play-off semi-final

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales Extra, Radio Cymru, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Wales are without nine regular members of their squad for the next stage of their bid to reach a first World Cup.

Olivia Clark, Poppy Soper, Rhiannon Roberts, Hayley Ladd, Ella Powell, Laura Hughes, Mia Ross, Ffion Morgan and Ceri Holland - who has been Wales' most influential performer since the retirement of Jess Fishlock - are all absent through injury.

Aside from back-up keeper Soper, all those players would have been contenders to play some part in the two Albania ties.

The long list of absentees means there is a youthful look to Wales' squad, with six uncapped players and a number of others with minimal international experience involved.

Nevertheless, Wilkinson says Wales are well placed to cope thanks to their regular policy of inviting young players to train with her senior side.

"I think it would be silly for me to say that having nine injuries was predictable - I think that was out of the norm," Wilkinson said.

"If I could have had no injuries I would have, but equally this is football and we adapt and we are a small country.

"I don't think we can pretend that we have unlimited players, so the fact I'm able to put together a team of 23 that has such strength and with a lot of experience is a good thing."

Goalkeepers Soffia Kelly and Lucy Farrell-Shrouder, centre-back Cadi Rodgers, wide player Heidi Hills and forwards Casi Gregson and Olivia Francis are the six players with Wales in Albania who are yet to be capped.

Then there are the likes of Scarlett Hill, Phoebie Poole, Tianna Teisar and Chloe Williams who have only a handful of international appearances between them.

Wilkinson insists the various inexperienced players are "absolutely" ready if required in what are high-stakes games.

"They've trained with a great intensity, they've done their work off the pitch and really involved themselves in meetings," she added.

"They've done everything they can to put themselves in the best possible position to get minutes."

Wales focus on Albania as Grainger reunion looms

Wales' injury worries deepen as duo withdraw

Fishlock set for Wales return - but not as player

Wales topped their qualifying group courtesy of a rousing home win over the Czech Republic in the final game of that stage in June.

As well as cruising to victory over Albania, in Wrexham, they thumped Montenegro in their home group fixture.

Yet Wales' away form was nowhere near as convincing, with draws against the Czechs and in Montenegro either side of their triumph in Albania.

The Albanians are ranked 68th in the world, 37 places below Wales, but Wilkinson expects another stern examination against "a team that really knows what their strengths are".

"I think we I've spoken quite honestly [about how in] the second group game against them, they definitely could have scored at least once or twice," she added.

"I expect it to be a resilient performance from both teams, to stick in it and try to bring our best versions of ourselves. They give everything for their badge like we will for ours, so it'll be a tough match."

The prize on offer against Albania is a two-legged World Cup play-off final against either Norway or Romania in early December.

If they get that far, Wales would start as underdogs against Gemma Grainger's Norway side.

At this stage, Wales do not know if wins over Albania and Norway would be enough to seal a World Cup place.

There will be eight European play-off winners, with seven progressing straight to Brazil and one – the lowest-ranked nation from the group stage of qualifying – going into inter-confederation play-offs next February.

When asked whether the play-off process should be simpler, Wilkinson said: "This is above my pay grade. What I will say is it doesn't help to get stuck in what could be or what comes afterwards.

"There's different scenarios here, but it's not for us to change that.

"For right now, this is our path and we'll just keep taking care of what's in front of us one step at a time."

Suspended fine for Xhaka over Covid-19 certificate
description: Sunderland captain Granit Xhaka says he has received a suspended fine of 150,000 Swiss francs (£136,000) for obtaining a forged Covid-19 vaccination certificate.
fullText:
Sunderland and Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka says he has received a suspended fine of 150,000 Swiss francs (£136,000) for obtaining a forged Covid-19 vaccination certificate.

The 34-year-old, who is alleged to have obtained the certificate in 2022 when it was a requirement in Switzerland for some travel abroad, says the fine is suspended for two years provided he does not commit any further offences, and that he has already paid the court costs.

"A few weeks ago, I spoke personally here and said that I would take responsibility for my decision. I stand by that," the midfielder wrote in German on Instagram.

"I was sentenced by summary judgment for obtaining a false certification to a suspended fine of 50 daily rates of CHF 3,000 [£2,726] each.

"I accept the decision and take responsibility for my actions. Thank you for the many messages of support over the past few weeks. They mean a lot to me."

Xhaka was playing for Arsenal in 2022 and posted a statement on social media on 21 September saying he had a "mistrust" towards the vaccine and that he had been "influenced by worries and uncertainty".

He is Switzerland's record appearance holder with 152 caps and, following his initial statement, withdrew from his country's camp for their Nations League matches against Scotland, North Macedonia and Slovenia in the international break that has just concluded.

The Swiss office of public health had confirmed that while there was never a general legal requirement to obtain or hold such a certificate, it was needed for access to various activities, venues and travel, meaning that participation was restricted for anyone who did not possess one.

These measures in Switzerland were in place until the spring of 2022. After that point, Covid-19 certificates continued to be issued, primarily to enable members of the public to meet entry requirements when travelling abroad.

Xhaka captained Switzerland at the World Cup earlier this year, where they were knocked out in the quarter-finals by eventual runners-up Argentina.

He is expected to return to action when Sunderland host Brighton on Saturday (15:00 BST).

Black Cats boss Regis le Bris said: "No comment on external topics but [from] what I've seen during the international break, he has trained really well. It's positive. He's in a good place football-wise and for me that is the most important."

title: 'It's changed my life' - Eckert on Spygate scandal
description: Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert says the Spygate scandal is an experience that has changed his life.
fullText:
Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has said that Spygate is an experience that has changed his life.

The 33-year-old faced the media for the first time since being given a six-week suspended ban and a £28,000 fine by the Football Association (FA) for his role in the scandal.

Saints were expelled from the Championship play-offs in May after admitting spying on training sessions involving Oxford United, Ipswich Town and Middlesbrough before the play-off semi-final.

But Eckert escaped any individual punishment that threatened his job following an FA investigation into his conduct that lasted for more than four months.

The FA had proposed a three-month ban, but the commission gave credit to him for what they called "considerable mitigation in this matter, most particularly around the genuine contrition".

The governing body is still yet to confirm if it will appeal the independent commission's ruling.

"It's tough. It changes your life. If I would say it's been all easy, it's not," Eckert said.

"But you have to find a way. You have to come to a conclusion at one point in the summer of how you want to continue.

"That first decision [public backing from the owner] was not for me but for the club. And at that very moment, then it's for me to see if I have the energy to be the right one to bring that project forward.

"Once you make that decision, there's no excuses."

Eckert was in a relaxed mood during Thursday's media conference at the club's Staplewood training ground, sharing a joke with reporters before sitting down to answer questions.

Eckert free to stay as Southampton boss as Spygate ban suspended

New Eckert deal should be 'high on agenda' - Beattie

Time to draw line through Spygate - Parkinson

Saints face bitter rivals Portsmouth on Sunday (12:00 BST), and when he was asked about what kind of an atmosphere he is expecting, a grin broke out on his face before responding.

Although Wednesday's ruling was a positive outcome for Southampton and Eckert, there was a lot of negative reaction online from supporters of other sides who felt the punishment was too lenient.

Before the verdict, Cambridge United head coach Neil Harris told BBC Radio 5 Live that the Saints head coach "should get a ban and a huge ban".

Eckert admitted it was not just a relief for him to be able to finally bring an end to the case after more than four months of intense scrutiny and criticism, but also to those in his inner circle, personally and professionally.

"It's not just good for me [that it's over]," he added.

"I am not the one who shares too much from my private life but obviously it does make a big difference that we can draw a line, not just for me but also for the ones close to me.

"I'm grateful for the club, I'm grateful for the people close to me to help me throughout some moments that haven't been easy.

"And you just come to the moment now luckily where it's done and for us to look forward and that we get back to the performance that we need if we want to play for big goals this season."

title: Spurs' Simons enrols at iconic university Harvard
description: Tottenham's Xavi Simons enrols at prestigious American university Harvard as he continues his recovery from a long-term injury.
fullText:
Tottenham midfielder Xavi Simons has enrolled on a course at prestigious American university Harvard while he continues his recovery from a long-term knee injury.

The 23-year-old Netherlands playmaker has been sidelined since rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament in April - an injury that forced him to miss the World Cup.

Simons has now joined, external Harvard's Crossover into Business programme, a course tailored for professional athletes to develop their commercial skills.

The online course pairs athletes with Harvard MBA students to mentor them through practical case studies and enterprise management.

"I'm going back to school," Simons wrote on LinkedIn.

"During my recovery, I've been trying to use my time in the best way possible. Football is still my main focus, but I also want to keep learning and improving away from the pitch."

Simons recently travelled to the United States to step up his physical rehabilitation while visiting Harvard's campus in Boston.

"Getting back on the pitch is still my number one priority," Simons added.

"At the same time, I want to use this period to keep learning and invest in myself beyond football. Looking forward to getting started."

title: Cummins not worried about potential Khawaja revelations
description: Pat Cummins confirms he has spoken to Usman Khawaja about his former team-mate’s upcoming autobiography but the Australia captain says he has no concerns about potential sandpapergate revelations.
fullText:
Pat Cummins has spoken to Usman Khawaja about his former team-mate's upcoming autobiography, but the Australia captain said he has no concerns about potential sandpapergate revelations.

On Friday, Australia will begin their first Test series in South Africa since the ball-tampering scandal erupted in Cape Town in 2018.

At the time, captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and batter Cameron Bancroft were banned for their part in the plot.

Since then, the four Australia bowlers who played in that match, including Cummins, have denied they had any prior knowledge of the plan to cheat.

The quartet, who released a joint statement about the episode in 2021, are once again set to be united in the first Test against South Africa in Durban.

Khawaja played in all four Tests in 2018 and retired from international cricket in January. His autobiography will be released in November.

"Uz gave me a buzz a few weeks back that he is releasing a book," said Cummins. "He didn't go into too much detail, just basically gave me the heads-up that he is doing a book and, as always, no worries.

"Tell your story. It's fine. It's obviously a long time ago and all the investigations, everything was done back then and we answered every question a million times.

"It was dealt with then and all I can say is that as a group, we have moved on and we are very happy with the last eight to nine years how we have been as a group and evolved and obviously my focus is on captaining the cricket team."

At the time of the ball-tampering controversy, Smith explained it was devised by the "leadership group" of the Australian team on the third day of the third Test in Cape Town. Bancroft was caught rubbing sandpaper on the ball the same day.

While Smith, Warner and Bancroft – all batters – were punished, there was never an explanation of how bowlers Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon did not notice a change in the state of the ball.

In a 2021 interview with the Guardian, Bancroft was asked if the bowlers knew and replied: "It's pretty probably self-explanatory."

How an 'absolute fluke' exposed sandpapergate scandal

Test cricket's biggest scandals - your results revealed

Days after Bancroft's interview was published, Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and Lyon released their statement which said: "We feel compelled to put the key facts on the record again.

"We did not know a foreign substance was taken onto the field to alter the condition of the ball until we saw the images on the big screen at Newlands.

"And to those who, despite the absence of evidence, insist that 'we must have known' about the use of a foreign substance simply because we are bowlers, we say this: The umpires during that Test match, Nigel Llong and Richard Illingworth, both very respected and experienced umpires, inspected the ball after the images surfaced on the TV coverage and did not change it because there was no sign of damage.

"We respectfully request an end to the rumour-mongering and innuendo. It has gone on too long and it is time to move on."

Earlier this week, left-arm seamer Starc referenced the scandal when he said: "What's left to come out after eight years?"

And, speaking on Thursday, Cummins said the episode was "a long time ago".

"It's nothing new," the 33-year-old told ABC. "We've spoken about it a little bit. If the crowd gets rowdy or whatever, if someone needs an extra helping hand, we're around.

"To be honest, it's so long ago and we, as a group, move on from things pretty quickly. It hasn't taken up too much of our time."

The trip to South Africa is the first in a year of high-profile away series for Australia. After what appears to be a stern challenge against New Zealand in their home summer, Cummins' men then travel to India and defend the Ashes in England next year.

With all-rounder Cameron Green ruled out because of injury, the tourists are likely to choose between Cooper Connolly and Nic Maddinson for a place in the middle order.

On a Durban pitch expected to turn, South Africa have included two spinners – Keshav Maharaj and Simon Harmer - in their XI.

title: Ticket rises and more TV packages - why is price of sport increasing?
description: The price of sports tickets and TV subscriptions are on the rise - so what is behind the increases and how are they justified?
fullText:
At least £115 to watch a day of the Ashes in Birmingham - unless you are an Edgbaston member.

A minimum of £255 for a standard seat at the Wimbledon singles finals.

Prices starting from £289 for general admission to the British Grand Prix at Silverstone on raceday.

Those are the ticket fees British sports fans have been told a single adult must pay if they want to attend some of the country's most beloved sports events in 2027.

The cost of entry to elite sport in the UK has risen sharply in the 2020s, but attendances across the majority of sports are as strong as ever.

Even for armchair fans watching at home, the breadth and expense of television subscriptions can be a barrier to accessing sport.

So what exactly is behind the rise in prices, can the increases possibly be justified and what does it all mean for fans?

In a new BBC Radio 5 Live programme - The Price of Our Sport - BBC Sport has taken a look.

Fans reacted with anger when some of the ticket price rises for major events next year were announced earlier this summer.

The increase in Ashes ticket prices is stark - the minimum price the last time Edgbaston held a Test in 2023 was £65, a rise of £50 to £115 in just four years. Admission to other venues, including The Oval, is even higher.

Last time out in Australia, some seats were sold to fans at all five venues for between £16 and £22.

At Wimbledon next year, the most expensive standard seat for both the men's and women's singles finals will be £400, £50 more than 2026, and more than double the cost from 2017.

That still makes Wimbledon the cheapest of the four Grand Slams, but even a Centre Court ticket for the middle Saturday of the tournament now costs at least £130.

General admission for Grand Prix Sunday at Silverstone is up to £289 from £189 in 2021, while the cheapest allocated seat now costs at least £609, up from £276 five years ago.

And general admission to the 2027 Ryder Cup at Adare Manor, in the Republic of Ireland, will cost €499 (£434), compared with up to €260 (£220) in Italy in 2023.

And other events which took place this year laid bare just how much more fans are being charged.

Fans paid £150 to attend a day of The Open at Royal Birkdale earlier this year, compared to £95 at St Andrews in 2022.

Prices for the FA Cup final varied from £50 to £285 in 2026, compared with £50 to £120 in 2016.

"It's just ludicrous," says Lee Hanlon, an England cricket fan who lives close to Edgbaston, but has decided not to attend next summer's Ashes because of the price rise.

"I'm angry. It seems like a lot of the normal cricket fans have been priced out. It seems like just people with money are going now.

"The increase is just too much. I find it upsetting."

But for event organisers, the prices chime with wider trends.

"We exist in an experience economy - we have definitely seen a subtle shift in the value people are placing on belonging, on the atmosphere you can be part of when you attend a live experience," says Mark Darbon, chief executive of the R&A, which operates golf's Open Championship.

"So when we set our prices we start by looking at some of the other major sporting events and benchmark ourselves, on price and value for money, by looking at what others are delivering."

In a poll on the BBC Sport website, 95% of respondents voted that tickets for the 2027 Ashes were too expensive.

A spokesperson for Edgbaston said: "Our entry-level ticket prices roughly match inflation compared to the last time Australia visited Edgbaston in 2023 - but like the rest of the country, we're battling increased costs and trying to manage these wherever we can."

Whether prices are set by governing bodies or the stadiums, the costs of putting on a major sports event include things like utilities, staffing, technology, insurance and marketing.

The Open offers half-price tickets for attendees aged 16-24, and free tickets for children.

"Ticketing revenue generates less than 20% of our total revenue from The Open," Darbon says.

"We have seen really significant cost inflation in recent years. It now costs us 25% more than it did five or six years ago to host The Open - that could be £10-12m in incremental costs. We have to cover those costs."

Many prestige events and newly built venues also include an increased proportion of hospitality ticketing, which can drive up costs for fans wanting standard tickets.

"We are seeing more and more regular people willing to pay for a special experience at sport," says Richard Flint, chairman of Seat Unique, an online platform specialising in hospitality and VIP ticketing for events.

"Corporate boxes are being broken down more and more into individual seats, so it's less about people taking 10 of their colleagues and more about a couple, or four people, going together.

"[Teams and leagues] want to grow their revenue off the back of it, undeniably. Premium is much more open to people or go to one or two games a year, or who have travelled from abroad to come.

"Sometimes stadiums need updating and the revenue from premium ticketing can help fund a new stadium or new stand, so there are benefits to the everyday fan."

In a world with increasingly volatile economics and changing consumer habits, broadcasting live sport has been one of the more reliable ways for companies to generate revenue.

And live sport - and entertainment - is one of the few industries whose financial success is unlikely to be significantly compromised by artificial intelligence in the coming years.

That means more and more companies have taken an interest in buying the rights to show sports events, which means more TV subscriptions than ever before are necessary for fans wanting to watch all of the action.

A football fan in the UK, for example, must 

And they must pay for an annual TV licence to watch other matches on the BBC and ITV.

Without taking advantage of special offers, other sports can require even more subscriptions and even more money.

"It certainly helps when you can say to a fan that they only need to buy one subscription to see everything in one sport," says Pete Oliver, CEO of growth markets for DAZN, a global sports streaming service.

"If a sport is very fragmented, we would say it's not going to be a great proposition for the fan [for us to be involved], and it's probably not going to be a great commercial prospect for us.

"The cost of entertainment [subscriptions] generally will increase over time.

"There is natural inflation in the market, there is a lot of competition for sports rights, the athletes want to be paid more money, and the leagues want to do what is right for them, and if they can get somebody to pay more for the content, they will"

In some sports, including Premier League football, the money which leagues and clubs are earning from TV rights is by far their biggest source of income, but has plateaued to an extent in recent years.

So broadcasters are not necessarily always shelling out significantly higher costs for rights, but fans are still being charged more to watch.

Increased competition, growing operational costs and an uncertain long-term financial model all play a role.

"I think in the short term, the fans who are not going to illegal solutions are going to pay more to watch sport," says Pierre Maes, author and consultant in sports media rights.

"But we have reached a kind of roof - people have to pay a lot [and] we know that higher prices and more fragmentation leads to more piracy.

"People seem to have no moral obstacle to going with piracy. You can say that's bad, and that it's theft, but the reality is that people don't care.

"The music industry had to deal with this problem. In the long term, I think there is no other path than a Spotify of sports.

"Otherwise, sports will lose their fans and lose their attention."

title: Infantino given re-election boost as Montagliani seeks final Concacaf term
description: Gianni Infantino's chances of being re-elected as Fifa president appear to have been given a major boost as Victor Montagliani wants to remain as Concacaf chief.
fullText:
Gianni Infantino's chances of being re-elected as Fifa president appear to have been given a major boost after potential rival Victor Montagliani confirmed he wants to remain as head of Concacaf.

The Canadian, 61, was widely seen as a possible candidate after Infantino's failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors sparked a global backlash.

However, Montagliani never confirmed he wanted to challenge Infantino, and according to sources, he has now told colleagues that he will instead seek a final term as head of the confederation which governs North and Central America and the Caribbean.

As first reported by the Guardian, it means he will not stand against Infantino, 56, who has confirmed he will be seeking a fourth term in March's presidential election.

The rebellion against him, spearheaded by European governing body Uefa, must now try to identify a unifying candidate by the deadline of 18 November.

Meanwhile, Aleksander Ceferin will stand for a fourth term as Uefa president.

Ceferin informed delegates of his decision at a meeting of all 55 national association chiefs in Berlin.

Uefa also reaffirmed its opposition to Infantino as it published a 14-point plan to reform world football's governing body.

Ceferin's move had been widely anticipated and reverses his insistence he would not seek re-election, which the Slovenian outlined in February 2024.

At that point Ceferin, who was initially elected in 2016, was embroiled in a row over Uefa changing its statutes to allow him to serve for a fourth term.

However, there had been a growing expectation the 58-year-old would stand.

This has only been made more likely since Uefa launched its efforts to oust Infantino, who scrapped his sell-off plan following widespread opposition.

"I want to thank the national associations for their trust," Ceferin said.

"We have faced extraordinary challenges over the past years, and we have faced them as one team. There is still important work ahead, and I have therefore accepted their request.

"My ambition remains the same: to keep European football united, make our game stronger and leave Uefa ready for the next generation."

Ceferin has ruled out standing against Infantino himself but is committed to finding a candidate around which the game can unite in March's FIfa election.

Uefa and 54 of its national associations, Azerbaijan being the exception, agreed on a clear direction for Fifa reform as part of the meeting.

As yet, no confirmed candidate has emerged to challenge Infantino in March.

Former Tottenham Hotspur and Switzerland defender Ramon Vega says he intends to stand but it is unclear whether he can even garner the five letters of support required to get on the ballot paper.

"Institutional reform will not, on its own, be enough," Uefa said.

"Fifa also needs new leadership: a respected and unifying figure, deeply rooted in football, with the vision and experience to lead, the ability to command confidence across regions and an unequivocal commitment to development, reform, integrity and independence."

Much of Uefa's plan centres around institutional governance and removes some of the direct powers of the president, which led to the creation of the Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal behind closed doors.

It also said that presidential or executive interference must be removed from oversight bodies which cover ethics and disciplinary matters.

Uefa added that no Fifa resources should be used for personal or electoral interests, and that at least $10m (£7.5m) of additional funding should be made available to each of the 211 member associations.

title: Russell to take further grid penalty this season
description: George Russell says he will be taking a further grid penalty this season in addition to the one he has been hit with for the Singapore Grand Prix.
fullText:
George Russell says he will be taking a further grid penalty this season in addition to the one he has been hit with for this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix.

The Briton will start Sunday's race from the back of the grid because he needs to fit a new engine which takes him beyond his permitted number for the season.

But he says that he will have to take another new engine, as soon as a planned upgrade is ready, to get him to the end of the season.

Russell said: "You get (a limit of) four engines a season, so six races on each, and we have seven races to the end. So I will be taking another penalty, so yeah it's pretty relentless at the moment."

Russell's engine failure in Malaysia scuppered Mercedes' previous plan for him to last out with his older engine until the upgrade was ready, most likely for the next race, the United States Grand Prix in Austin.

F1 heat hazard declared for fourth time this season

Russell to start from back of Singapore grid after penalty

"I knew I was going to have a penalty," Russell said. "The plan was always to go in Austin, and obviously Singapore is the second hardest track to overtake on on the calendars. So you would never choose to do it (here).

"But we have no engines because of all of the various failures, so there was no engine I could have reverted to from earlier in the season. With the failure I had to take it.

"We don't have the (upgrade) this weekend, and because there are seven races remaining, you can either choose to roll the dice and hope it lasts for seven races, but also suffer a performance offset (as the engine degrades), or just accept I'll be taking another penalty."

Antonelli will also likely have another back-of-the-grid penalty when the upgraded engine is introduced, following his previous one at the Italian Grand Prix, which he won from 19th on the grid.

Russell will also be reverting to an older specification car in Singapore this weekend.

Mercedes introduced an aerodynamic upgrade in Malaysia last weekend, but it did not give the car the performance uplift expected.

So in an attempt to prove whether that was because of idiosyncrasies to do with the Sepang track or a problem with the upgrade itself, Mercedes is splitting the specification of their cars.

Russell will drive the specification with which he won in Azerbaijan, the week before Malaysia, while Antonelli will run the new spec.

Russell said: "I actually asked a question already on Friday in Sepang. At the end of the day it's the car I'm reverting to is a car that was on pole by 0.8secs and Kimi won the race before, so it's important to remember the context. It's not like reverting back to a launch car.

"Given the circumstances of the grid penalty as well, it just seemed like a no-brainer. For me, unfortunately we're not going to be fighting for a podium this weekend, it's exceptionally unlikely, so it's more important for us to try and understand, was Malaysia a one-off or was it the upgrade?"

Live commentary on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra; live text updates on BBC Sport website and app

Russell's retirement in Malaysia, along with Antonelli finishing second to Red Bull's Max Verstappen, meant the Italian's lead in the drivers' championship has extended to 84 points.

Both Mercedes drivers have suffered reliability problems this year but Russell believes his season has been disproportionately affected by factors outside his control.

"I've probably had more failures this year than I've had in the three seasons put together, and of course it's tough to take," he said.

"If I'm being 100% fair with myself, as I've said before, the performance this season hasn't been strong enough, and it probably would have affected me more if I'd have still been in the fight.

"But obviously the pressure and the momentum, every setback has an impact on that momentum.

"Since the start of the year (an engine failure) in Canada was the big one, and then, you know, the drive-through penalty in Monaco. The loss at the weekend has basically compromised two weekends for me.

"Two races, Silverstone and Spa, with the PU issues we had (involving a loss of performance from the engine), it's been pretty incredible how things have panned out this year, but I think just focus on what you can control."

title: Maresca says 'feeling is fantastic' among Man City squad
description: Enzo Maresca says his players "don't care too much about the noise" surrounding Manchester City over the 115 Premier League charges.
fullText:
Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca says the "feeling is fantastic" among his players and they "don't care too much about the noise" surrounding the club after it was found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges brought against it by the Premier League.

The club's international players returned to training on Thursday, nine days after the Premier League published a damning report that stated the club had used "sham" contracts to disguise secret funding of more than £830m.

BBC Sport reported this week that Maresca would address the players upon their return to domestic duty after news of the verdict broke while the majority of the squad were away with their respective nations.

It is understood the City head coach asked his players not to allow the crisis that has engulfed the club to affect their attitude and focus as the Premier League campaign gets back under way this weekend.

"The feeling is fantastic, to be honest," Maresca said in an in-house interview when asked about the mood among his squad prior to their trip to face Liverpool on Sunday (16:30 BST).

"The players are excited for the next two games. But especially they are excited because in this moment we are top of the league. The players are just focused on that.

"They know what we can control is the football side - they are not worried at all about different things.

"They know their profession and they know that the noise is there, but they don't care too much about the noise. They are just focused in this moment on how we can beat Liverpool and how, together with the fans, we can try to win in Anfield."

Maresca added he felt "calm" and his squad trusts the club "completely".

City have launched an appeal and have publicly maintained their innocence.

The private communication to those with links to the playing staff at City has been equally as emphatic, it is understood.

Speaking to Sky Sports, striker Erling Haaland echoed his manager's sentiments, saying: "I care a lot about this place. I spent my first four years here, it's a special place for us. I care a lot about City and the fans. I am a fan myself. I feel with them.

"The fans will have a good time on Sunday - we have to stick together. We have to stay with each other and stay positive. No matter what happens in life, we always have to smile. Stay positive, look ahead, and try to win football games and enjoy the situation.

"We have to stick together and spread the love to each other. Enjoy the ride and smile."

What Guardiola said about Man City charges

Clubs fear political interference in Man City appeal

Manchester City vs The Premier League

As Premier League football returns following a three-week hiatus, managers of rival clubs can expect to be asked to comment on the City verdict during their compulsory pre-match press conferences.

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner will face the media on Friday but told reporters earlier in the week he hopes the process is completed "as soon as possible".

Glasner joined Forest from Crystal Palace in the summer and cited his experience of the latter's demotion from the Europa League to the Conference League in 2025 after the club breached multi-club ownership rules.

"Let's wait until the final verdict is spoken, but my wish is just that this is quick," Glasner said.

"Because we didn't know with Palace if we were in the Europa League or Conference League and then it was 'you will hear on Thursday' and then that became Monday, because it was always delayed. Then we got the final verdict 10 days before the Conference League started.

"That's why I think this must be [completed] as soon as possible.

"There is still damage for the Premier League, not just in England. It's a big topic all over the world, especially in Europe.

"The most important thing is the integrity of the league because as soon as the fans can't trust it, they won't watch it any more."

Some manager news conferences were held on Thursday and Leeds head coach Daniel Farke and Newcastle's Matthias Jaissle both steered clear of commenting at length on the matter.

It is understood a number of clubs have already taken a clear stance for their managers not to comment.

Coventry boss Frank Lampard - who played for City in the 2014-15 season - said the players will not feel they have lost their titles even if the club is stripped of them because it is part of their personal history.

City have yet to be punished but BBC Sport has been told there has been little appetite from within the Premier League - both the organisation and its clubs - for past titles to be taken from them.

"I have titles and I don't have my titles hanging on my wall at home, I have them in my head," said Lampard, who won the Premier League three times with Chelsea.

"You are competing against the best in the Premier League and a lot of things are out of [your] control but you are competing against the best and they're very hard to win.

"So I think it would be very hard to take someone's title away as a player individually as they should be in your head as opposed to in a beautiful glass cabinet or whatever. I know there are some who do that."

Lampard made 38 appearances and scored eight goals when he joined City in 2014 after 13 years at Chelsea.

title: Six Alabama players to watch vs. Georgia football
description: A big contest is set to take place in Tuscaloosa between Georgia and Alabama. Who are players to watch for Alabama against UGA?
fullText:
The Georgia Bulldogs (5-0) will be on the road this weekend heading into a very hostile environment in Tuscaloosa to face the Alabama Crimson Tide (5-0). You could start to feel the energy in Athens for Georgia fans as soon as the page was turned after the Vanderbilt win last weekend. The Georgia-Alabama game has huge implications in the SEC and simply because it is Georgia vs. Alabama. Both teams will bring a physical style of play and a lot of speed into this contest.

Each and every season both Georgia and Alabama have deep rosters and at every single level they are ultra-talented. Alabama has a young signal caller in Keelon Russell and Georgia has a fifth year veteran in Gunner Stockton. Both quarterbacks have been playing nearly flawless up to this point along with other players across the depth chart.

Alabama football returned 13 total starters heading into the 2026 season after losing 15 starters. It has shown to be a next man up mentality and Georgia will be able to match their talent up against the Tide's talent.

Let's take a look at six of Alabama's key players heading into the Georgia-Alabama game this weekend.

Keelon Russell has emerged into one of the best quarterbacks in the country early on. Russell seems to be comfortable and because of that, Russell has been lighting it up through the air and on the ground. The dual-threat signal caller has 1,414 passing yards, 11 touchdowns and four rushing scores through Alabama's first five games.

Ezavier EJ Crowell is an outstanding back who is a five-star freshman who is going to be a major force this season for the Crimson Tide. He brings a great balance for Alabama and they can rely on this freshman to make the plays needed coming out of the backfield. Crowell has 204 yards rushing and three touchdowns on 26 carries in five games.

Another electric playmaker for the Crimson Tide is Trae'shawn Brown. Brown is a guy who is a playmaker that can score at any time during the game. He is someone who is going to make the most of every opportunity with the ball in his hands. Brown has 211 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 42 carries through the first five games.

Ryan Coleman-Williams is one of the best wide receivers in all of the nation. Coming out his freshman season with a big-time breakout season as a 17-year old star, Coleman-Williams earned first-team All-SEC and freshman All-American honors with 48 receptions for 865 yards and eight touchdowns.

His sophomore year, he struggled a bit due to injuries and leading the nation with 13 dropped passes and only hauling in four touchdowns all year. For the 2026 season, Coleman-Williams has added 15 pounds of muscle and trained at a high level in order to take his game to another level. Coleman-Williams had an incredible touchdown grab in the first-half of the Mississippi State game.

Luke Metz has been an outstanding linebacker early on for the Crimson Tide as he leads the unit with 36 total tackles. Metz brings energy, physicality and toughness to the Alabama defense especially in the linebacker core.

Keon Sabb is a former Michigan Wolverine who was apart of the 2023 national championship team. Sabb brings a high level of play and experience into the secondary at Alabama especially at safety. He will continue anchoring the top of the secondary.

Alabama has all of the players to make things tough for the Georgia Bulldogs. This will certainly be a challenge and the same goes for Alabama. This contest will be the biggest yet for both programs and if history serves us well, this one will be a dandy of a game.

Kickoff between Georgia and Alabama will be Saturday, Oct. 10, 7:30 p.m. ET.

title: CBS Sports grades Falcons' first four games of 2026 season
description: Falcons earn impressive quarter-season grade from CBS Sports
fullText:
Four games into the season, the Atlanta Falcons look more dangerous than they have since the 2017 season, which was the last time they finished with a record over .500. At 2-2, they're tied with the Carolina Panthers at the top of the NFC South - but technically in second place due to Carolina's Week 2 win in Atlanta.

That's still a hell of a lot better than we expected them to be after the dismal showing we saw in the first two games of the season. Other analysts have taken notice, as well.

According to Zachary Pereles at CBS Sports, the Falcons deserve a B+ grade for their first four games.

"Bijan Robinson looks like the best running back we've seen in a long, long time, and Penix looked more comfortable in his second start than his first. For as much love as the offense deserves, defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich deserves just as much, working with a unit dealing with injuries across the board. The Falcons are second in defensive success rate and first in both yards per rush allowed and pressure rate. Unfortunately, we do have to factor in the two games started by Cooper Rush, but this team's arrow is very much pointing up as long as Penix can stay healthy."

That 0-2 start may yet come back to haunt the Falcons if the divisional race comes down to the wire. For now, this looks like the best - and most complete team in the NFC South, even if they got thrashed by Carolina just a few weeks ago. The Panthers have been decimated by injuries since then and their underperforming defense gives them an imbalanced look.

Meanwhile, the Falcons have the best run game in the league, an explosive passing game with Penix healthy and a defense that's performing light years ahead of any reasonable expectations going into the season.

Much of the credit must go to head coach Kevin Stefanski for putting together an excellent staff, where offensive coordinator Tommy Rees, offensive line coach Bill Callahan and defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich are all doing magnificent work in their respective roles.

A win over a likely Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore Ravens team on Sunday night would give Atlanta a ton of momentum going into the toughest stretch of their season, where they'll four contenders in five games going into their bye week.

title: Colin Cowherd reacts to Broncos’ ‘dink-and-dunk’ offense with Bo Nix
description: Colin Cowherd feels that "everything looks hard" for Bo Nix following his recent performance. Will the Broncos' QB bounce back this week?
fullText:
When teams win in the NFL, the quarterback gets a good portion of the credit. When they lose, they take a good portion of the heat. Right or wrong, that's the way the game has always been.

Following their most recent loss, the Denver Broncos still have a major problem at quarterback, according to some in the media and many fans within Broncos Country. In their 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, Bo Nix completed 25 of 42 passes for 214 yards with one touchdown.

While the Broncos may not have lost because of Nix, he certainly didn't lead his team to a win, and he is facing major scrutiny following this performance.

The way Bo Nix played cost the Broncos a win over the 49ers! | @bstokley14 and @JVtakes with @markschlereth pic.twitter.com/DiP2LPIVPz

Meanwhile, others are still firmly behind him.

If you want off the Bo Nix bandwagon... JUMP! | @JoshuaDover and @CecilLammey pic.twitter.com/YaG0gTaNCu

Meanwhile, Colin Cowherd, host of The Herd on FS1, who regularly goes back and forth on Nix and the Broncos in general, had this to say on his show:

"Everything with Bo Nix looks hard. He's not throwing the ball down the field... It looks so EASY for Brock Purdy."@colincowherd breaks down why Nix & Purdy are on different levels pic.twitter.com/4D0J2ekbey

"I liked Bo Nix out of Oregon because he had 61 college starts, Sean Payton liked him too, there was a little Drew Brees," said Cowherd on The Herd. "But when RJ Harvey is your top receiver against the Niners, it's a problem".

After discussing why he has changed his mind on Nix, Cowherd went on to say this:

"Everything with Bo Nix looks hard. He is averaging fewer air yards per attempt in the NFL this year, 5.4 yards, that's the lowest since the stat's been tracked. What does that tell you? He's not throwing the ball down the field. Marvin Mims, has he disappeared? This is dink and dunk and behind the line of scrimmage."

Cowherd then discussed how much easier everything looks and feels for a guy like Brock Purdy while placing much of the blame for the Broncos' offensive ineptitude at the feet of Nix.

"Everything for Bo Nix is underneath. Anything downfield looks so incredibly hard, and he is such an ineffective quarterback in the first half, it puts you in a hole," said Cowherd.

It seems Cowherd shares many of the same frustrations watching Nix operate within this Denver offense as many of the fans inside Broncos Country did on Sunday. Perhaps more criticism needs to be on the starting quarterback for his performance and not as much on the first-year offensive coordinator for calling the plays.

Either way, the Broncos need to figure out how to get Nix into more of a groove before the season takes a turn for the worse.

title: F1 Drivers Speak Out After the FIA Finally Explains the Bahrain GP Software Crash
description: The FIA has officially concluded its investigation into the chaotic software failure that brought the relocated 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix to a sudden, crawling halt. According to the governing body, a massive coding bug was triggered when cars dropped to…
fullText:
The FIA has officially concluded its investigation into the chaotic software failure that brought the relocated 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix to a sudden, crawling halt. According to the governing body, a massive coding bug was triggered when cars dropped to low engine RPMs inside specific track sectors where a 250kW power reduction was mandated for the wet-weather conditions. This specific combination caused the cars to permanently lose power until the FIA rushed an emergency code update to the grid.

While the unprecedented digital blackout frustrated fans, the drivers actually sitting behind the steering wheels offered a surprisingly nuanced perspective ahead of the Singapore Grand Prix Sprint weekend.

During the official media day at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, drivers were asked by Nelson Valkenburg (Via Play) if they finally feel in control of the complex 2026 engine regulations after the disastrous Sepang incident. For Haas F1 Team driver Esteban Ocon, the Malaysia failure was just a minor bump in the road compared to the absolute nightmare of early-season testing.

"I think, honestly, compared to testing, things have changed, you know, so much," Esteban Ocon explained. "I remember testing the first time I drove the car…. had no deployment. 80% of the laps that I was doing in Barcelona, it was, you know, quite complicated. And we didn't really understand why that was happening."

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA – OCTOBER 04: Max Verstappen of the Netherlands driving the (3) Oracle Red Bull Racing RB22 Red Bull Ford Powertrains leads Lewis Hamilton of Great Britain driving the (44) Scuderia Ferrari SF-26 and Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy driving the (12) Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team W17 on the formation lap during the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 04, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Joe Portlock/LAT Images) // Getty Images / Red Bull Content Pool // SI202610040284 // Usage for editorial use only //

When reflecting specifically on the formation lap chaos at the Sepang Circuit, Esteban Ocon admitted the sudden loss of power was highly confusing, prompting him to try and manually trick the engine into delivering forward momentum.

"This was unexpected for everyone," Esteban Ocon stated. "I started to feel like, yeah, I'm racing because, you know, I was just cutting the lines, trying to do the last metres. I was thinking of maybe upshifting to second, staying on idle to, you know, get more speed compared to the others."

Despite the chaos, he expressed confidence in the governing body, adding, "I'm sure the FIA is on top of it now, so it should be okay."

Alpine F1 Team driver Franco Colapinto echoed those exact sentiments, noting that the entire paddock has been forced to adapt to the wildly unpredictable nature of the 2026 power units.

"I think during the whole year, it improved a lot. It was very inconsistent at the start. It was tricky for everyone to understand," Franco Colapinto told reporters.

He emphasized that massive technical overhauls always come with unexpected growing pains, regardless of how much simulator preparation is completed.

"I think, again, problems and issues we'll still get, and things that we don't know and understand will still happen," Franco Colapinto noted. "But the important thing is we learn from it and get on top of what happened last week, for example."

KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA – OCTOBER 04: Max Verstappen of the Netherlands driving the (3) Oracle Red Bull Racing RB22 Red Bull Ford Powertrains leads Liam Lawson of New Zealand driving the (30) Visa Cash App Racing Bulls VCARB 03 RB Ford on track during the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on October 04, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Photo by Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images) // Getty Images / Red Bull Content Pool // SI202610040283 // Usage for editorial use only //

For seasoned veterans like Aston Martin driver Fernando Alonso, the digital drama was practically a non-issue. Because the Aston Martin garage managed to avoid the wet-weather glitch entirely, the two-time champion was completely unfazed by the software panic.

"In our case, last week, the car was fine," Fernando Alonso shrugged. "So we didn't suffer any of the issues. So difficult to comment." He added that the entire grid now expects the problem to be fully understood and resolved moving forward.

To ensure the multi-million-dollar grid doesn't crash again, the FIA confirmed that the emergency code configuration utilized in Malaysia will remain fully active for the Singapore Grand Prix. A permanent, fully tested wet-weather software patch is scheduled to be released ahead of the United States Grand Prix in Austin later this October.

title: Two Colorado defenders rank among Big 12's leading tacklers
description: Colorado safety Randon Fontenette and linebacker Gideon Lampron are two of the Big 12's tackle leaders heading into the Buffaloes' Week 6 bye.
fullText:
The Colorado Buffaloes have two defenders near the top of the Big 12's total-tackles standings heading into their bye week, with Randon Fontenette and Gideon Lampron continuing to handle a significant workload in Chris Marve's defense.

Fontenette has 40 tackles, placing him second behind Iowa State's Sullivan Schlimgen, who has 46. Lampron has 38, sharing third place with Cincinnati's Antwan Peek Jr. Those rankings reflect season totals, with Fontenette averaging eight tackles per game and Lampron averaging 7.6 through five appearances.

Fontenette supplied an important defensive play on Texas Tech's opening possession after halftime Saturday, sacking Will Hammond for an 11-yard loss and forcing a punt while Colorado held a 7-3 lead.

His production against Texas Tech also came with costly penalties during the Red Raiders' go-ahead touchdown drive. A pass-interference call and a personal foul extended the possession, underscoring the need for better discipline from one of Colorado's best defenders.

Fontenette's ability to finish plays has made him a consistent presence around the ball, and avoiding those penalties will give Colorado better value from him on defense.

Lampron delivered one of Colorado's biggest stops in the second quarter, meeting Quinten Joyner for no gain on fourth-and-one at the CU 7-yard line. The turnover on downs preserved the Buffaloes' four-point lead.

He added a tackle for a 5-yard loss in the third quarter after a Colorado turnover gave Texas Tech possession at the Colorado 31-yard line. That disruption helped force the Red Raiders to settle for a field goal.

Lampron now has 5.5 tackles for loss, adding backfield production to his tackle total. With Tyler Martinez likely out for the season, Colorado will continue to rely on his experience as the linebacker rotation adjusts ahead of Utah.

title: Campo Verde flag heads to California to play No. 1 team in the nation
description: Campo Verde is headed to Southern California to play JSerra Catholic on Oct. 9, the consensus No. 1-ranked team in the country.
fullText:
Gilbert Campo Verde is about to play one of the biggest games in Arizona high school flag football history.

Campo Verde is headed to Southern California to play JSerra Catholic, the consensus No. 1-ranked team in the country, on Friday, Oct. 9. JSerra (22-0) is ranked No. 1 by both USA TODAY and MaxPreps. Campo Verde (4-1) is ranked No. 11 by USA TODAY.

Since the season-opening loss to Gilbert Highland on Sept. 15, which also is nationally ranked by USA TODAY and MaxPreps, the Coyotes have been on a roll, winning the last four games by a combined score of 264-0. Senior quarterback Amaya Moreno, considered one of the top quarterbacks in the nation, looks dialed in.

"We're feeling good," Campo Verde coach Brian Coger said. "We got a good game plan, we believe. We understand the talent there. We respect everything they've done. But it's one of those things where we have to go into it with confidence as well, and that's what we're doing.

JSerra has been just as dominant and is coming off two recent big wins in a row, against Sierra Canyon and Mater Dei. Both of those schools are in the MaxPreps top 25.

"We're gonna have to shut down a few of their plays they tend to lean on from what we've seen," Coger said. "Honestly, we just got to stick to our game plan. If we do that, we should be fine."

This game was specifically scheduled by Coger, as he tries to raise the national profile of his team.

"We want to test ourselves," Coger said. "We want to go out and try to find the toughest competition that we can find and see where we are nationally."

Campo Verde features some of the top players in Arizona, with Moreno, sophomore wide receiver and defensive back Jaiyana Bogan-Jacobs and junior wide receiver and defensive back Claire McMahon.

Moreno is currently ranked third in the state with 1,484 passing yards and is second in passing touchdowns with 24. Bogan-Jacobs — who is the No. 2 basketball prospect in the country in the class of 2029 — has been a force on both sides of the ball, with 29 receptions for 496 yards and eight touchdowns on offense and two interceptions on defense. McMahon has 21 receptions for 389 yards and six touchdowns on offense, to go with three interceptions on defense.

In the past, there have been big out-of-state games for Arizona flag football teams. The sport is only in its fourth season since being sanctioned by the AIA in 2023. Chandler Hamilton traveled to Ohio for a national tournament in 2025. Gilbert Highland won the Tampa Flag Football World Championships in January. But both of those games were out-of-season, and Highland was playing as a club team against other clubs.

This matchup is arguably the biggest in state history, considering the national pedigree. The stakes are high. An Arizona school is playing the top-ranked flag football team in the country. It's California versus Arizona. It's also a homecoming for Coger.

"We take a lot of pride in it," Coger said. "Especially for me, being originally from California (Inland Empire) and now being out here. I like to go back home and show them what we can do out here in Arizona."

title: Dodging snakes and jumping lizards: Bottas’ ride to Singapore
description: Valtteri Bottas revealed his battles with wildlife after cycling from Malaysia to Singapore for this weekend’s race. The Finnish driver arrived in Singapore on Wednesday after completing the epic 419km ride, opting to ditch a flight for his bike following last weekend’s Formula One round in Sepang.
fullText:
Valtteri Bottas revealed his battles with wildlife after cycling from Malaysia to Singapore for this weekend's race.

The Finnish driver arrived in Singapore on Wednesday after completing the epic 419km ride, opting to ditch a flight for his bike following last weekend's Formula One round in Sepang.

Cadillac driver Bottas' journey involved cycling in darkness and he brushed off some close encounters with wildlife along his route.

"I saw some snakes, which I was a little bit worried about, but actually, they were pretty chill. They were just doing their thing," he said.

"I saw one cobra, one python just crossing the path in front of me. I saw some of those big lizards that you also see here, one was on the path.

"I had to jump over it on a bike because I saw it last minute. I got chased by one dog, I got stuck behind a group of cows on one small track.

"The wildest part was the riding at night in the jungle. The noise in there, your mind starts to play games.

"'What is out there? Who knows what is out there?' But then you just need to crack on and keep going."

During McGuire's tenure with the Bobcats, the Fresno State product averaged 3.3 points, 3.8 rebounds, 0.8 assists and 0.6 blocks in 52 games as a small forward. McGuire would play for the Golden State Warriors during the 2011-12 season and three different teams during the 2012-13 season before his NBA career came to an end after six seasons. title: Leaked MLB memo provides blueprint for owners’ behavior during lockout
description: Enjoy October MLB baseball while it lasts as MLB owners formalize lockout plans, and some are downright petty
fullText:
As MLB fans enjoy October baseball and the forthcoming World Series, owners are already putting plans in place to deal with the pending lockout effective December 2.

The owners perhaps have learned from the last lockout in 2021-2022 how to do things better, or in some cases be more petty.

The Atlantic obtained a copy of a MLB memo that outlines how owners should behave and what to expect when the lockout occurs.

MORE: Big Papi, Tampa Bay Rays roast Yankees after ALDS loss

Oct 7, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago White Sox pitcher Mike Vasil riles up the team before game three between the Cleveland Guardians and the White Sox in the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Rate Field. Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The two sides can co-mingle at offseason weddings; however, no one can talk about baseball or the lockout.

Presumably, the two parties are allowed to be photographed together at these events, but that detail was not divulged.

MORE: Brewers' Garrett Mitchell robs Padres' Manny Machado with all-time catch

If owners and teams want to send players' Christmas cards, they must be mailed before the lockout goes into effect on December 2.

This seems like a minute detail that someone thought was important, but in the scheme of things, seems like a silly and unnecessary rule.

Player images will disappear from MLB websites on December 2 with one noteworthy exception. MLB stores will continue to be allowed to display and sell players' jerseys on team websites.

None of these behaviors seem helpful in problem solving and getting the two sides to an agreement to avoid a delayed start to the 2027 MLB season. It seems like things are bound to get worse before they get better. Everyone needs to enjoy October baseball to its fullest because with these plans in place, it is unclear when we will see MLB baseball again in the future.
