title: Mohammed Shami’s India return? R Ashwin drops major hint after Bhuvneshwar Kumar comeback
description: Ravichandran Ashwin hints at the potential recall of Mohammed Shami to the Indian cricket team. This speculation comes after changes in the selection committee, especially with Ajit Agarkar stepping down. The reintroduction of Bhuvneshwar Kumar suggests a trend towards prioritizing seasoned players. Shami's remarkable performances in domestic cricket may enhance his chances of making a return after his absence since the Champions Trophy 2025.
fullText:
Mohammed Shami could soon find his way back into the India squad, according to former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin, who believes the change in the selection setup may open the door for the veteran pacer.

India recently announced their squad for the upcoming five-match T20I series against New Zealand, which follows the ongoing T20I series against the West Indies. The biggest talking point from the selection was the return of Bhuvneshwar Kumar to the national side after a four-year absence.

The squad was also the first selected after Ajit Agarkar completed his stint as chief selector. With Agarkar no longer part of the setup, Ashwin feels India could be moving towards a greater reliance on experience, particularly with Jasprit Bumrah's workload being managed regularly.

Speaking on his YouTube channel Ash Ki Baat, Ashwin suggested that the change in approach could benefit Shami as well.

"The chairman of selectors is set to be changed. Ajit Agarkar is no longer a part of the setup. Maybe Ajit focused more on youngsters and newcomers. But now you see, without Bumrah, India's bowling attack can be a little susceptible. The BCCI is now leaning towards experience. The fact that they have picked Bhuvneshwar (Kumar), I wouldn't say that the door is shut on (Mohammed) Shami either. But I am extremely happy that Bhuvneshwar has broken down the door for his selection," Ashwin said.

Shami last represented India in the Champions Trophy 2025 final against New Zealand in March last year. Since then, the pacer has not been selected to play for India in any format.

His absence from the national side had also led to repeated exchanges between Shami and Agarkar over his non-selection. Agarkar had previously indicated that Shami was not fully fit, but the pacer showcased his fitness by playing domestic cricket and regularly picking up wickets.

The 35-year-old has an extensive international record, having played 64 Tests, 108 ODIs and 25 T20Is for India. He has taken 229 wickets in Tests, 206 in ODIs and 27 in T20Is.

With Bhuvneshwar's return signalling a possible shift towards experience, Ashwin believes Shami's return may not be far away either.

title: Juventus Could Lose Yildiz with Another Subpar Season
description: Juventus repelled every offer for Kenan Yildiz last summer, but the situation could change in a year’s time if they miss out on the UEFA Champions League again. Their owner will offset the losses wi...
fullText:
Juventus repelled every offer for Kenan Yildiz last summer, but the situation could change in a year's time if they miss out on the UEFA Champions League again. Their owner will offset the losses with another capital increase. The club would have to solve its financial woes on its own if another subpar campaign followed, Corriere dello Sport reports.

Selling the Turk would lead to a mammoth profit, as the Bianconeri value him at north of €100M. It wouldn't be hard to find deep-pocketed suitors. Real Madrid have been following him for a couple of years. If there's an opening, they'll focus on him and Erling Haaland in the future. Bayern Munich have been tracking his growth ever since the Bianconeri poached him from their youth academy a few years back, and Arsenal have shown interest more than a few times.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio (via Bet365News), Yildiz leaving Juventus could be one of the surprises of the next windows. The Gunners and Tottenham tendered large offers in the recent past, but they weren't even considered.

If it were to happen, the Old Lady would look to cash in a fee closer to €150M than to €100M. In addition, their management's early move to secure a potential heir, Kerim Alajbegovic, could be telling.

His injury can lead to forgetting his value and importance. Their owner has routinely fueled the self-financing narrative but then eventually always poured money into the club to keep it competitive. Selling their best player would go in the complete opposite direction, even if it'll be tantalizing for particularly rich figures.

title: Haliburton has happy Hilton Homecoming
description: In his first basketball game in 472 days – June 22, 2025 – the two time Iowa State letter winner and Olympic gold medalist contributed seven points and six assists in a 123-112 win over the Timberwolves at Hilton Coliseum. “I think it’s obviously the loudest preseason game I’ve ever been a part of,” Haliburton […]
fullText:
In his first basketball game in 472 days – June 22, 2025 – the two time Iowa State letter winner and Olympic gold medalist contributed seven points and six assists in a 123-112 win over the Timberwolves at Hilton Coliseum.

"I think it's obviously the loudest preseason game I've ever been a part of," Haliburton said following the game. "Probably be the loudest preseason game I've ever been a part of, but had a lot of fun. A lot of special memories I've made here and that just adds to it." So, it was a lot of fun.

Prior to Wednesday night's preseason contest, Haliburton spent 16 months recovering from a severe Achilles tendon rupture suffered during Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals in Oklahoma City. Reflecting on the physical and mental hurdles, Haliburton responded to praise from Pacers coach Rick Carlisle regarding his consistency throughout the rehabilitation process.

"I don't know if I could give you one word to really summarize it, but it's been a roller coaster," Haliburton said. "Roller coaster of emotions for me. I've had a lot of hard days, but I think it's all just part of it being a human being, and 16 months is a long time. I've never went that long without playing basketball. So, I feel like I learned a lot about myself."

He added that sitting out forced a shift in his overall perspective.

"I got to spend a lot of time on the sideline watching and even today as I was like struggling to start the game and I was tired as hell," Haliburton said. "But even through that I just kept feeling like, 'Man, I'm playing again,' like how thankful I am. So I think my perspective on life on basketball has changed a lot through this injury. I think that's the biggest thing is it's been easier for me to take a step back and be like, 'Just appreciate the little things right now.' So that's what I'm doing. Just appreciating all the things that come with this, the good and the bad, and continuing to learn, and been fun."

Once back on the floor, Haliburton admitted his adrenaline was surging. After turning the ball over on Indiana's initial possession, he quickly settled in by hitting a 15-foot jumper for the Pacers' first points of the night. He later knocked down a 3-pointer and celebrated by raising his palms upward.

"When you miss some time and you come back, I think from any length of time, that your timing and all those things have to get better," Haliburton said. "For me, I feel like I'm just playing really fast right now. I mean, it's first game, but slow down. I think it was just a lot of adrenaline. I was hyped to be out there, excited, but I just got to slow down a little bit."

He compared his return to the adjustment period faced by league newcomers. "Just felt like I was, like when you talk to a rookie or something and they say like the game's just moving really fast for me right now," Haliburton said.

"I don't think my reads were moving fast necessarily as much as just I was moving really fast. I just got to slow down, but it'll happen with time and the only way to really replicate that is game reps against other guys and that's what that was. So really excited about it, and there's a ton of improvement that there is to be made on my end and on our team's end, but just excited to be back on the floor."

He expressed confidence moving forward.

"As I slow down a little bit, I'm able to get my feet under me to shoot the three to get downhill, kind of hit him on that late roll," Haliburton said. "It'll come with time, but I'm really confident in it. I know how good of a player he is and we all are, but I mean, we all were at halftime like, 'This is going to be a lot of fun,' So, we know we all got to get a lot better and we will as the season goes on, but it's been enjoyable."

The matchup came together in part due to Haliburton's relationship with Minnesota star Anthony Edwards.

"Shout out to Ant because, like obviously me wanting to do this, Timberwolves got to say yes," Haliburton said. "They're not saying yes without his approval and that's like my brother. So I made sure to tell him I appreciate him. If he wants to go to Georgia, I'll make sure that we say yes to that as well. So I'm just really appreciative of him and the whole organization."

Pregame anticipation made sleeping difficult prior to tipoff.

"I enjoyed it a ton. I was really excited," Haliburton said. "I think all day, I struggle to sleep a little bit like anybody when the season starts. I'm always like that. I'll chill, man. I just was excited to be back here. I knew it was going to be crazy. I don't think I was prepared for exactly how loud it was going to be. But that's the fun part about it. Why I love this place… just I'm excited that there's film on tape, like I'll be able to watch film, good and bad. I'm excited about that. Just the process that comes with being great. So, looking forward to all of that."

However, Haliburton kept the exhibition setting in perspective.

"I think it'll be different come game one of the real season," Haliburton said. "Preseason's kind of like an open scrimmage to a sense. I think it was less excitement about being back on the floor and more excited about being back at Iowa State because I view this as just my first time playing against other guys, but I really don't think I'll feel the whole all the weight of it until game one of the real season."

During the game, Iowa State fans booed Pacers rookie guard Braden Smith, who played collegiately at Purdue, finished with a 3-pointer, five assists and five rebounds in 14 minutes.

Haliburton admitted he was puzzled by the reception.

"I still don't really understand the reason. A little dumbfounded," Haliburton said. "I mean, I get it, but I mean, for lack of a better, we beat the [ out of Purdue last year, so it ain't like he did anything crazy to us last year. So, I don't understand. That's tough to play your first game in like a college road environment. How weird is that?"

Haliburton praised Smith's floor vision, including a highlight behind-the-back pass.

"I thought he did a great job," Haliburton said. "He settled into the game really well. I'm sure he will tell you that the game was moving really fast for him, but as time goes on, he's able to slow down. I mean, Braden's an unbelievable passer, has unbelievable feel for the game. So, that behind the back pass he had was really—I thought that was dope… As time goes on, I feel like he gets more reps in the G-League and in preseason and in the league, I feel like he'll be really good. So, I was proud of him… I apologized. I was like, 'I don't know why they're booing you. Who knows?' But I thought he did a good job."

Haliburton also reflected on the 2020 NBA Draft class, which featured four top-12 selections on the floor in Wednesday's game. "I don't think we talked about it," Haliburton said. "I think we all kind of feel like, they thought our draft class was going to be terrible, and I feel like I played with half of our draft at this point. But I think we understand the magnitude of it, how cool it is. Obviously the NBA is a brotherhood, there's only so many of us, and I tweeted when LaMelo got traded there how cool that is, for two of the top 2020 guys to be together and how exciting it is. I've had the opportunity to play with Aaron and Obi and Sticks and James Wiseman and a couple guys… I think it's really cool seeing them drive. Obviously they're in the other conference and I'm really excited for them."

Although Haliburton sat out the second half, he actively engaged with the crowd, joining in on "Juicy Wiggle" and singing along to "ISU Fights"

"I'm a Cyclone through and through, being a part of something like that is a lot of fun," Haliburton said. "Just being a part of all the traditions."

When asked about participating in student fan traditions such as singing along to Mr. Brightside, Haliburton joked: "Yeah, don't worry. I'm not a student anymore. I can't get in trouble."

"It was a lot of fun, man. I enjoy coming back here. I enjoy all of our traditions here and the culture of Iowa State," Haliburton added. "When I came here, I really immersed myself in it. I went to every football game. I went to the women's basketball games. I went to gymnastics meets. I went to everything and I think that was just the exciting part of being a Cyclone and that's what comes with it."

He underscored the unique connection between university athletics and the local Ames community.

"We don't have any professional sports teams here," Haliburton said. "So, we kind of all are the professional sports teams. I think all the athletes here take pride in that and that makes a lot of fun."

On the floor, Aaron Nesmith paced six Pacers in double figures with 19 points. Jay Huff scored 16 points, Ben Sheppard added 13, and Obi Toppin and Pascal Siakam finished with 10 points apiece.

Indiana continues its preseason schedule Saturday, hosting the Keshon Gilbert and the Atlanta Hawks at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. The Pacers travel to face Oklahoma City on Tuesday before concluding preseason play against Milwaukee on Friday, Oct. 16.

Regular-season action begins Oct. 21, at New Orleans.

title: Ella Toone: Manchester United star handed dream England news – official
description: Manchester United forward Ella Toone has been handed a surprise call-up to the England squad, it has been confirmed.Initial setbackToone was one of the high-profile absentees from the original England...
fullText:
Manchester United forward Ella Toone has been handed a surprise call-up to the England squad, it has been confirmed.

Toone was one of the high-profile absentees from the original England squad that was named by Sarina Wiegman.

She missed out, alongside other key stars such as Chloe Kelly, Aggie Beever-Jones, Lotte Wubben-Moy and Taylor Hinds. United endured a tough start to life under new boss Eva Olid, although they now appear to have turned a corner and are back on the right track.

Talking about the decision to omit Toone and Kelly last month, Wiegman said, "The main reason is I think the levels weren't what I expected from them on the pitch."

"I've had conversation with them and there's a big competition going on too. It's been a very hard decision for both of them."

"I really believe in them. They're not in the squad, but I believe in them. We follow them and we expect a bit more. We know they can bring more. That was the message again too. There's also competition going on."

She added, "I hope they can step up and show what they can do because I'm convinced that they can do better. I think they are convinced about that too. I think they took the feedback in a positive way, but it's hard to [hear] at the same time, of course."

Toone has now been called up to replace the injured Lucy Bronze.

Toone will link up with her international teammates ahead of the upcoming FIFA Women's World Cup qualifiers.

The two-legged European play-off will take place against Greece, with the winners then due to face Slovakia or Ukraine. Bronze has withdrawn due to injury.

Bronze sustained the issue during Chelsea's WSL victory over West Ham on Sunday.

Other United stars in the squad are Jess Park and captain Maya Le Tissier. Toone has already won 69 caps for her country, since making her debut in February 2021.

title: Sepang’s F1 Return Proves One-Stop Races Are Dead
description: Sepang's thrilling F1 return shows fans crave tire battles, not one-stop processions. Max Verstappen's win proves variable strategy is the only future for the sport.
fullText:
The one-stop race is dead. Max Verstappen's victory in Sepang on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026, proved that fans want tire wear and strategy, not just fast laps. Beyond The Flag reports that the weekend's excitement delivered precisely what Formula 1 fans desire to witness. This single event in Malaysia has changed the entire conversation about the future of the sport. We do not need more boring processional races where drivers make one stop and drive to the finish line. We need the chaos that Sepang delivered.

The evidence is clear in the numbers. Lewis Hamilton took only two pit stops during the race. In stark contrast, Sergio Perez needed seven stops to finish. That massive gap in strategy created the drama that modern fans crave. Per Beyond The Flag, the race was a massive success because drivers had to spontaneously modify race strategies. When bad weather hit and tire degradation became uncertain, teams gambled on their plans. That gamble paid off for the viewers at home. It also paid off for the sport's long-term health.

The success of this one-off race has already secured a permanent return for the Malaysian Grand Prix. Malaysia's prime minister confirmed discussions with F1 regarding Sepang's permanent return to the calendar. This is a huge win for the sport. It shows that when you put the right track on the calendar, the fans show up. The prime minister's confirmation means the days of a one-year trial are over. Sepang is here to stay.

This shift also opens the door for other tracks that have been sitting on the sidelines. Tracks like Mugello, Nürburgring, Hockenheim, and Kyalami might seek permanent reinstatement on the F1 calendar soon. Significant changes are planned for the 2027 schedule, featuring long-awaited returns by Portugal and Turkey. The dominoes have started to fall. Sepang was just the first piece.

Success stems from a race featuring abundant action and fluctuating tire degradation. Such events remain more dynamic than those requiring just one or two stops due to low degradation. The weekend in Baku the week prior saw very little tire degradation. Most drivers needed only one pit stop there. That race was fine, but it lacked the edge that Sepang provided. Fans know the difference. They feel it in their bones when the strategy is flat versus when it is wild.

The benefit is clear globally, leaving only the finer details to resolve. This recent Sepang event could enable circuits currently absent from the schedule to finally return in the future. The sport does not need to be perfect. It needs to be unpredictable. Max Verstappen's win on Sunday was the first win of the season for the Red Bull driver, but the real victory belongs to the format that allowed it to happen.

title: Walsall have done OK but need to be better - Grant
description: Walsall head coach Lee Grant says his squad know they have to keep getting better after their unbeaten start to the League Two season.
fullText:
Walsall boss Lee Grant says their encouraging start to the season has not altered the view that they have to get better heading into the resumption of their League Two season.

The unbeaten Saddlers won three and drew five of their eight games before the three-week international break and go to Fleetwood Town on Saturday (15:00 BST), hoping to move into the top three in the table.

Grant arranged a behind-closed-doors friendly with Championship side Lincoln City this week to keep his squad sharp and he said that was excellent preparation.

"We at our stadium - that adds another layer to it - both teams are in kit, official EFL referees and they're [Lincoln] really good," Grant told BBC Radio WM.

"We had to work really hard and were challenged from the minute the whistle blew.

"I really like that for our group. I just like that mentality, that work is there, it won't it won't be diminished by whatever sort of performance comes from us [on Saturday].

"In the long term, that'll serve us well. It hasn't got in the way of us trying to improve and trying to move things forward.

"I'm really pleased and proud of the group the way they've gone after the last couple of weeks and looking forward to seeing how it does translate."

Walsall's three wins have come against Accrington and Port Vale at the Pallet-Track Bescot Stadium and an opening-day victory at Gillingham.

Home points have also been taken against Grimsby and Rochdale and on the road at Crewe, Exeter and Tranmere, in the last game before the international break.

Grant said he knows there is room for improvement.

"We're feeling like we've done some things OK, and there's a hunger to try to be better," he added.

"It's not one of these ones where I'm sitting here saying 'it's feeling really comfortable' because we've won games or we've not lost.

"We know we've got to be better. And the supporters will echo that.

"They've seen us play really well against Port Vale, and for a half at Crewe. They've seen us finish a game impeccably well at Gillingham but start the game a little bit chaotic so we know we can be more of what we want to be more often and more consistently and it's searching for that all the time."

title: Chiefs Star Patrick Mahomes Gets Encouraging News Involving Family Member During Bye Week
description: Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs head into their bye week as the last undefeated team in the AFC. The quarterback just led Kansas City to a 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Oct. 4, but the latest good news arrived off the field. A court ruling involving a close family member […] The post Chiefs Star Patrick Mahomes Gets Encouraging News Involving Family Member During Bye Week appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs head into their bye week as the last undefeated team in the AFC. The quarterback just led Kansas City to a 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Oct. 4, but the latest good news arrived off the field. A court ruling involving a close family member now offers the star some welcome peace of mind.

A Texas judge has approved limited travel for Patrick Mahomes Sr., who remains on felony probation. According to court documents obtained by TMZ Sports and reported by The Jasmine Brand, the 56-year-old former MLB pitcher asked to attend Chiefs games in Kansas City, Las Vegas and Cincinnati.

He can attend games at Arrowhead Stadium, but the requests for the October game in Las Vegas and the December game in Cincinnati were denied. He must also submit urine tests, requested by his probation officer, before and after each trip.

The filing shows progress as well. Mahomes Sr. has completed 160 hours of community service and an outpatient alcohol treatment program. His probation officer reported no violations on his SCRAM alcohol monitor.

The case stems from his February 2024 arrest in Tyler, Texas, which landed during Super Bowl LVIII week. In March 2026, his probation was extended by two years after a monitoring alert, but screening tests showed no signs of alcohol use.

In the docuseries The Kingdom, Mahomes Sr. said, "I made a vow that he would never have to deal with anything because of drinking, because of me."

That promise now meets a son who is flying high on the field.

Mahomes has guided Kansas City to a 4-0 start after recovering from serious ACL and LCL injuries. During Week 4 in Las Vegas, he threw for 225 yards and two touchdowns, both to Tyquan Thornton, and improved to 7-0 at Allegiant Stadium. Kenneth Walker III ran for 177 yards and two scores.

The Raiders pushed back late, and the pressure was heavy. Patrick Mahomes said, "I think you have to stay with it," when describing the back-and-forth game.

Wide receiver Rashee Rice left with a hamstring injury in the first quarter, so the bye week arrives at a useful time. Kansas City went 6-11 last season and missed the playoffs for the first time since 2014, which makes this fast start even more notable.

The Chiefs now rest before hosting the Los Angeles Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium on Oct. 18. The Chargers are winless through four games, and Mahomes Sr. is now cleared for home games like this one.

title: Yankees playoff history in Aaron Judge era: New York's poor results prove club is wasting slugger's prime
description: Despite having one of the greatest sluggers in baseball history, the Yankees haven't been able to break through with a title in the postseason.
fullText:
Yankees playoff history in Aaron Judge era: New York's poor results prove club is wasting slugger's prime originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

No matter how great one player is, it takes an entire organization to win a World Series title. From Ted Williams and Ty Cobb to Barry Bonds and Ken Griffey Jr., a long list of Hall of Famers and baseball superstars finished their careers without their team ever sitting on top of the throne.

If things don't change quickly for the Yankees, Aaron Judge may be in peril of joining that list of ringless legends. Judge, now 34, hasn't been healthy enough to play in New York's 2026 postseason run.

Now trailing the Rays in the ALDS, the Yankees are on the brink of another postseason exit in the Judge era — despite one World Series appearance and three ALCS berths, New York has consistently come up short.

Here's a look at the Yankees' postseason history with Judge over the past decade.

After missing the postseason in 2016, in Judge's rookie year, New York finished with a wild-card berth behind their young slugger's 52-homer season.

It wound up being one of the Yankees' deepest October runs of the Judge era. After beating the Twins in the AL Wild Card game and Cleveland in the ALDS, New York pushed the Astros to the limit, winning three consecutive games in the ALCS to take a 3-2 series lead.

Houston, though, rode Justin Verlander to a Game 6 win, then shut out the Yankees 4-0 in Game 7. After coming within a win of the World Series, the Yankees' season ended in the ALCS.

Despite winning 100 games in the regular season, the Yankees were a wild-card team in 2018, and their postseason run did not last long.

A lineup featuring six 20-homer-hitters fell to the eventual champion Red Sox in the ALDS after winning a one-game Wild Card matchup against the A's. In Aaron Boone's first season at the helm, New York had plenty of regular-season success, a potent lineup and a collection of veteran starters, but Boston won the ALDS in four games, including a 16-1 Game 3 win.

The Yankees won the AL East for the first time in the Judge era in 2019, winning 103 games to best their 2018 total. Again, they appeared set for a deep postseason run, sweeping the Twins in the ALDS to reach another ALCS against the Astros.

Again, however, the Jose Altuve-Gerrit Cole-Alex Bregman era Astros got the best of the Yankees. Houston won the series in six games, capped by Altuve's walk-off home run off Aroldis Chapman to win Game 6 and go to the World Series.

In the shortened 2020 season, the Yankees grabbed another wild-card spot after winning 33 of 60 games.

Their postseason result looked similar to prior years: a Wild Card sweep over Cleveland, but an ALDS loss to the Rays. In the decisive Game 5, Judge homered, but that was the Yankees' lone run as Chapman allowed a homer to Mike Brosseau in the eighth that ultimately won it for the Rays.

The Yankees grabbed another Wild Card spot in 2021 after a 93-win season. This time, though, they didn't reach the ALDS.

In the one-game playoff, Nathan Eovaldi went a strong 5.1 innings for the Red Sox, while Xander Bogaerts and Kyle Schwarber both homered in a 6-2 win for Boston.

For the third time in six years, the Yankees lost to the same pesky Astros squad in the ALCS in 2022.

This time, it wasn't particularly close. New York, which won 99 games in the regular season and beat the Guardians in the ALDS, was swept by Houston. Verlander, Framber Valdez and Christian Javier silenced the Yankees' bats, while Chas McCormick and Jeremy Pena both homered twice in the series.

The Yankees finally broke through to the Fall Classic in 2024, their first World Series appearance since winning in 2009 and first with Judge. But in a star-studded matchup, they couldn't quite get the long-awaited ring.

New York bounced back from missing the postseason in 2023 by winning 94 games and taking down the Royals in the ALDS, then Guardians in the ALCS. But the Yankees then ran into arguably the most dominant team in baseball of the era, the Dodgers.

Los Angeles quickly took a 3-0 series lead behind Shohei Ohtani, a Game 1 walk-off home run from Freddie Freeman, and strong pitching from Walker Buehler and Yoshinobu Yamamoto. By the time the Yankees won Game 4 with 11 runs, it was far too late.

The Dodgers took Game 5, 7-6, after scoring two late runs, with Ohtani winning his first World Series title.

Last year, the Yankees fell to an AL East rival in the postseason for the fourth time in the Judge era.

After Judge won his third MVP in the regular season, the Yankees did take down the Red Sox in the AL Wild Card series — partially due to a dominant Game 3 start from Cam Schlittler — but they didn't find as much success against Toronto in the next round.

Vladimir Guerrero Jr. led a dominant Blue Jays lineup to a 3-1 series win in the ALDS, sending the Yankees home early. In all three of Judge's MVP seasons (2022, 2024, 2025) the Yankees couldn't get him a ring.

For the first time in Judge's career, the star outfielder was too injured to appear in the playoffs. Nonetheless, the team fell in the ALDS in familiar fashion despite once again beating the Red Sox in the Wild Card series..

Like in the year prior, the Yankees were the top Wild Card team against a division rival who won the AL East, this time as the Rays were the best team in the AL. Tampa Bay's combination of strong pitching, contact and speed outclassed New York, who put on an error-fest in Game 2 on their way to a sweep.

The Yankees did get great performances from Ben Rice and Cam Schlittler in this run, perhaps signaling a new dynamic dup moving forward. Still, it was another example of the team falling short vs. a superior team.

title: Trieu: Michigan State visitors for Illinois game includes in-state targets
description: Michigan State will host a number of recruiting targets for Saturday's game against Illinois.
fullText:
Michigan State returns home this weekend to face Illinois.

The recruiting visitors list for the game includes four-star linebacker Allen Kennett V, who is coming all the way from California. The Anaheim Servite junior is looking heavily at schools in the Midwest, though. He visited Nebraska last weekend, Notre Dame earlier in the season, and will visit Michigan next month. Kennett was at MSU for a spring practice and has gotten to know head coach Pat Fitzgerald and the staff, particularly linebackers coach Max Bullough, well.

Warren De La Salle quarterback Grayson Thurston will be back on campus again after visiting for the Nebraska game. Thurston was offered by the Spartans in the summer after he camped there. Fitzgerald and quarterbacks coach John McNulty attended a De La Salle game earlier this fall.

Monroe Jefferson junior running back Drake Jones will be on campus. Jones plays multiple positions, including safety/linebacker on defense, but rushed for 1,500 yards as a sophomore and has put up big numbers so far this season. His 6-foot, 205-pound frame makes him project well to the tailback position in the Big Ten.

Spring Lake Park (Minnesota) junior Kaden Konkler is a multi-talented recruit the Spartans staff has uncovered. Konkler can play safety or wide receiver in college. He has size at 6-foot-3, 200 pounds, while running 4.57 in the 40-yard dash. He caught seven touchdowns as a sophomore. Iowa State and Minnesota also are recruiting him.

The Spartans will have a pair of young defensive tackles visiting in Birmingham Seaholm's Harrison Bowers and Lakewood (Ohio) St. Edward's Tyler Browne. Both are sophomores, but Bowers stands 6-foot-3, 275 pounds, while Browne is 6-foot-3, 294 pounds. That position is one where big, athletic bodies can be tough to find so both of these prospects are expected to be heavily recruited over the next two years.

Reynoldsburg (Ohio) linebacker Duane Greer, a 6-foot-2, 205-pound sophomore, will be on campus. Greer is an athletic two-way player who also makes an impact as a running back. Miami (Ohio) has extended an early offer.

Philadelphia Roman Catholic defensive end Victor Ezeukwu was offered by Michigan State to start the month of October.

Ezeukwu is an athletic 6-foot-5, 230-pound prospect with the kind of length and frame to be heavily recruited and highly ranked.

Vanderbilt, West Virginia, North Carolina, Boston College, Cincinnati, Duke and others have offered.

Allen Trieu covers Midwest football recruiting for On3. He has been featured on the Big Ten Network on its annual Signing Day Show. His Michigan and Michigan State recruiting columns appear weekly at detroitnews.com.

title: ‘Not a Surprise’ — Aaron Rodgers’ Ex-Teammate Spills the Beans on Steelers QB’s and Mike McCarthy’s Tense Relationship
description: The heated argument between Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy caught fans’ attention on Thursday night during Pittsburgh’s 27–24 loss to the Cleveland Browns. Rodgers and McCarthy had an argument, as Rodgers was seen frustrated while waiting for the play call. Meanwhile, McCarthy appeared to respond with strong language of his […] The post ‘Not a Surprise’ — Aaron Rodgers’ Ex-Teammate Spills the Beans on Steelers QB’s and Mike McCarthy’s Tense Relationshi
fullText:
The heated argument between Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy caught fans' attention on Thursday night during Pittsburgh's 27–24 loss to the Cleveland Browns.

Rodgers and McCarthy had an argument, as Rodgers was seen frustrated while waiting for the play call. Meanwhile, McCarthy appeared to respond with strong language of his own, immediately turning the moment into one of the biggest storylines surrounding the Steelers.

During a recent episode of ESPN's "Big Day", analyst and former NFL player, Jeff Saturday, shared his view on the controversy. Having worked closely with both Rodgers and McCarthy, Saturday explained that this was not the first time the two had experienced tension and said:

"I played under McCarthy and with Aaron. And so, this is not a surprise. I mean, we can church it up however we want. The facts are this is not the first time they've been upset with each other."

"You're trying to get something effectively communicated that's not being communicated effectively," Saturday said. "And all of a sudden, everybody feels pressure. Everybody's intense."

"The level of intensity for you and I sitting here and all these cameras in our faces and then them sitting in that moment with the pressure building, it is a completely different mindset."

“I played under [Mike] McCarthy and with Aaron [Rodgers] and so this is not a surprise.”

—@SaturdayJeff on the confrontation between the Steelers' HC and QB pic.twitter.com/hfDuN0fe9B

— Big Day (@BigDayESPN) October 6, 2026

Based on Saturday's comments, it looks like Rodgers and McCarthy can survive an angry exchange. Pittsburgh needs the two to make their communication work before the play clock turns another disagreement into prime-time television.

The situation also highlights the unique dynamic between Rodgers and McCarthy, who already share a long history from their time with the Green Bay Packers. Their previous working relationship included both significant success and moments of disagreement, making their reunion in Pittsburgh particularly interesting for NFL fans.

The sideline drama should not get in the way, as the Steelers' main goal is to win games. Both Rodgers and McCarthy have to bring their best to the team, while maintaining open communication and controlling their emotions. If they can do that, it could benefit the organization and help the Steelers remain focused on their ultimate goal.

With the season still developing, every possession and decision will carry added importance. The current controversy has highlighted one important condition for the Steelers to succeed: McCarthy and Rodgers have to be on the same page. There will be situations that require quick decision-making and effective communication, and the organization needs both the quarterback and head coach to demonstrate teamwork, especially when the pressure is at its highest.

title: Jason Kelce shares insight on former Philadelphia Eagles teammate Lane Johnson’s retirement
description: Future Hall of Famer Lane Johnson announced his retirement from the NFL earlier this week. The Philadelphia Eagles will now be without their star offensive lineman for the first time since drafting him in 2013.
fullText:
Future Hall of Famer Lane Johnson announced his retirement from the NFL earlier this week. The Philadelphia Eagles will now be without their star offensive lineman for the first time since drafting him in 2013.

Johnson earned six Pro Bowl selections and five All-Pro honours during his career, and he won two Super Bowls with the Eagles (LII and LIX). Philadelphia won 66 percent of the games he played in, compared to just 38 percent of the games he missed.

The 36-year-old will be remembered as one of the greatest offensive linemen of his generation, and few know him better than Jason Kelce. His former Eagles teammate has now shared some insight into what Johnson may be going through following his retirement.

Jason Kelce, a former member of the Philadelphia Eagles' NFL-leading offensive line with Lane Johnson, knows how difficult retirement can be. While he appreciated the opportunity to leave on his own terms, it did not make his decision easy.

Kelce revealed that he spoke to Johnson before his own retirement in 2024, and more recently, about Johnson's retirement. He explained the challenge Johnson would have faced to play another season without being 100 percent focused, suggesting he made the right decision.

"This was his 14th season," Kelce said. "Whenever you get older, it's something you think about. I certainly thought about it for the last four years before I ended up making the decision.

"It becomes really hard to play football when you're on the north side of 35 years old, especially up front at the offensive line position. You're playing through things and your life is changing. There's a lot going on.

"I remember talking to Lane for many years about when it was right for me to stop playing. We've certainly had those discussions with Lane before…

"He's one of the few players who was so good that everyone is still chomping at the bit to get him to play. The reality is that if you're not 100 percent in, this is a sport that's very hard to do, and I trust that he felt it was the time to stop."

title: Nick Young explains why LeBron James and Kobe Bryant are ahead of Michael Jordan in the GOAT debate
description: Nick Young had the chance to play with Kobe Bryant and against LeBron James, and considers both of them better players than Michael Jordan. Young was on the Lakers during Bryant’s final years in the NBA.
fullText:
Nick Young had the chance to play with Kobe Bryant and against LeBron James, and considers both of them better players than Michael Jordan.

Young was on the Lakers during Bryant's final years in the NBA. As for his battles with LeBron James, he got to witness The King's excellence during the 2017 NBA Finals when he played for the Golden State Warriors.

Both Kobe and LeBron are considered two of the greatest players ever, along with Michael Jordan. But Young thinks they are both better than His Airness.

Speaking on Shannon Sharpe's Club Shay Shay podcast, former NBA champion Nick Young explained why he has LeBron James and Kobe Bryant over Michael Jordan.

While his preference for Kobe Bryant is personal, he noted that James is a physical anomaly, and that no player could replicate the gifts or performances that he's exhibited, while he can't say the same for Kobe or Jordan.

Young said: "Kobe is my GOAT, because I was in that era, I'm from LA, I went to all the parades, and all that. But realistically, you have got to say LeBron is the GOAT, just because he can play one through five. Passing, scoring, and rebounding.

"Nobody is going to be 6'9, 260; you don't see that every day. I could be the same height as Kobe. Wade is the same height as Kobe and Jordan. I feel like it goes LeBron, Kobe, Jordan. I got Jordan third."

Young certainly makes a strong point about why LeBron James should be considered the greatest of all time, but for him to have Michael Jordan below Kobe Bryant makes little sense.

In almost every category, whether that be statistical dominance, championship success, or overall impact on the game, Jordan has the edge over Bryant.

The GOAT debate may never end, with fans of Michael Jordan and LeBron James arguing forever. But for Young, LeBron James is the best to ever play the game.

title: Dodgers NLDS notes: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dave Roberts
description: The Dodgers beat the Braves in four games to win the National League Division Series, and have advanced to their eighth National League Championship Series in the last 11 years with Dave Roberts at the helm. But before we dig into the celebration and aftermath from Game 4, here are a few leftover notes from […]
fullText:
The Dodgers beat the Braves in four games to win the National League Division Series, and have advanced to their eighth National League Championship Series in the last 11 years with Dave Roberts at the helm. But before we dig into the celebration and aftermath from Game 4, here are a few leftover notes from the Game 3 win.

Ken Rosenthal, who worked this NLDS for Fox, wrote at The Athletic how manager Roberts made a rare appearance in a pregame hitters meeting before Game 3. From Rosenthal:

Roberts wasn't thrilled with the Dodgers' offensive effort in Game 2 of the National League Division Series, a 3-2 loss to the Atlanta Braves. So, with the series tied and his team set to face one of the best pitchers in the sport, the manager wanted to send his hitters a message.

"It was just to kind of try to put them in a mindset that it's an elimination game, to challenge them to be more exhausted emotionally because they're playing every single pitch," Roberts said. "I wanted Chris Sale to know he was in a fight. I think we accomplished that."

Yoshinobu Yamamoto's latest brilliant postseason start on Tuesday earned the praise of Gabe Lacques of USA Today, who notes how Yamamoto is earning his place alongside many notable historical postseason stalwarts.

"Yama is the Dodgers' rock and his three-year exploits – a 2.14 ERA, 58 strikeouts to 13 walks in 63 innings – are, era-adjusted, growing just as impressive as the Koufaxes and Pettittes and Bumgarners," Lacques wrote.

Michael Baumann at FanGraphs extolled Yamamoto's effort in Game 3, and yet another appearance of October Kiké Hernández.

Molly Knight at her The Long Game newsletter also extolled Yamamoto's postseason prowess, calling him "an absolute playoff monster who can throw six different pitches for strikes in any count while never breaking a sweat."

title: Plymouth boss 'thrilled' to have MacKenzie fully fit
description: Plymouth Argyle boss Tom Cleverley is "thrilled" that defender Jack MacKenzie has returned to full fitness.
fullText:
Plymouth Argyle boss Tom Cleverley is "thrilled" that defender Jack MacKenzie has returned to full fitness.

The left-back completed 90 minutes for just the second time in his injury-hit career at Home Park in Tuesday night's Jersey Mike's Trophy penalty shootout win at Newport County.

The 26-year-old played 12 times in all competitions last season due to tendonitis in his knee and shin splints, and missed the early part of this season with an abductor injury.

But his first full game since the 2-1 win over Doncaster Rovers on 7 March proved to Cleverley that the former Aberdeen player is ready to go.

"He's one that we can really trust - everything from an environment and a values perspective is what I stand for," he told BBC Radio Devon.

"He's all in, he's serious about his job, he's aggressive, competitive and I'm thrilled to have him back and available from the start of every game now."

title: Rafael Benitez reveals why Steven Gerrard surpassed Ronaldo and Benzema as his greatest-ever player
description: Rafael Benitez has said former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard was the most complete player he ever coached, above Cristiano Ronaldo and Karim Benzema.Benitez worked with Gerrard for five seasons at ...
fullText:
Rafael Benitez has said former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard was the most complete player he ever coached, above Cristiano Ronaldo and Karim Benzema.

Benitez worked with Gerrard for five seasons at Anfield, with the pair winning the 2005Champions League and 2006 FA Cup together.

Gerrard was a huge influence on both triumphs, scoring in each final, and produced arguably the best football of his career under Benitez, winning the PFA Player of the Year and FWA Footballer of the Year awards.

Benitez has coached some world-class talent during a managerial career at some of Europe's top teams with spells at Valencia, Liverpool, Inter Milan, Chelsea and Real Madrid.

However, he said Gerrard was the number one player he coached. Discussing the midfielder in the recently releasedLiverpool's Greatest: A Celebration of 100 Reds' Stars book, Benitez said: "When I was at Real Madrid, they were asking me who is the best player I have coached, and I said Steven Gerrard.

"When we came to Liverpool, he was a box-to-box midfielder. The power, the potential. Then, tactically we were trying to manage. I think he didn't realise at this time, [it was] late on he realised what we were looking for.

"He has the power, he was good in the air, he could shoot with the right foot and the left foot, and he could pass, he could control the ball.

"So, he was a complete player that needed to understand a little more the game, the tempo of the game. These kind of things he was learning. That was the only thing he was missing at the beginning, because he has all the energy, all the potential.

"Later on, little by little, and especially when we signed [Fernando] Torres - because Stevie has a very good touch, it's precise and with power - and with Torres running, it was very difficult for defenders to stop him.

"He was very good doing almost everything. He has also stamina, he has commitment. I think he was great in terms of a key player for Liverpool and the way he was conducting himself on the pitch and outside the pitch. He was professional and he liked all the players to give everything.

"That is the reason why, for me, he is the best player I have coached. I had [Samuel] Eto'o, [Cristiano] Ronaldo, [Karim] Benzema - but he was more complete than all of them."

title: ‘Does Not Play on Time’ — Analyst Isn’t Sold on Kyler Murray As Vikings QB Despite Successful Run in 2026
description: Although the Minnesota Vikings have started strongly in the 2026 NFL season, questions about the starting quarterback’s future are still up in the air. Kyler Murray is back as the Vikings’ QB1, who was dealing with injuries during the second half of the 2025 NFL season, doesn’t seem like the longterm answer for the franchise […] The post ‘Does Not Play on Time’ — Analyst Isn’t Sold on Kyler Murray As Vikings QB Despite Successful Run in 2026 appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Although the Minnesota Vikings have started strongly in the 2026 NFL season, questions about the starting quarterback's future are still up in the air.

Kyler Murray is back as the Vikings' QB1, who was dealing with injuries during the second half of the 2025 NFL season, doesn't seem like the longterm answer for the franchise to some analysts.

In a recent episode of 'NFL on NBC', former Tennessee Titans general manager Ran Carthon shared his thoughts on the quarterback and said:

"It's just not a good fit. Yes. Kyler Murray does not play on time. Yes. This offense is built on playing on time, hitting guys in stride with the football, and we saw it once 'cause we made the comment, it's like he's dropping back 30 yards like we're playing Tecmo Bowl. You know, dropping all the way back to the end zone and looking for the open man. I don't… I've always felt like Kyler Murray, because of his size, I thought he had a unique skill to slide himself into throwing windows to allow him to be able to see it. For whatever reason, he's just not trusting what's going on in the pocket, and that's just his style of play now, and I just don't know that it fits in what KC wants to do."

The Vikings have won all four of their games, but their offense has not consistently matched the performance of their defense. In Minnesota's Week 4 victory over the Miami Dolphins, Murray became more effective late in the game and completed 13 of his final 14 passes.

Despite the concerns surrounding Murray's playing style, his performance during the Vikings' unbeaten start has given the quarterback an opportunity to silence his critics. Minnesota has shown that it can win games even when the offense is not operating at its highest level, which could take some pressure off Murray as he continues to adjust.

However, consistency will be important as the season progresses. As the season progresses, the organization will have to face tougher competition, and the veteran quarterback will need to deliver his best performances.If he can improve in those areas while maintaining his ability to create plays outside the pocket, Minnesota could have a legitimate chance to make a deep playoff run. For now, the quarterback remains one of the biggest storylines surrounding the undefeated Vikings.

Murray's ability to make plays with both his arm and legs remains one of the biggest advantages he brings to Minnesota. His mobility can create opportunities when the original play breaks down, while his experience gives the Vikings another weapon in critical situations. However, the quarterback will need to find a better balance between extending plays and operating within the structure of the offense.

For head coach Kevin O'Connell, getting Murray comfortable in the system will be crucial. Fans have high expectations for the organization, as the Vikings have clearly shown that they can compete at a high level. However, Murray's presence at quarterback could change the team's dynamics, while expectations will continue to rise as the season progresses.

title: Rangers boss McInnes 'not a fan' of extended break
description: Rangers manager Derek McInnes says he is "not a fan" of the extended international break which he considers "too long".
fullText:
Rangers manager Derek McInnes says he is "not a fan" of the extended international break which he considers "too long".

The Ibrox club had 13 players away on duty for their countries after the Scottish Premiership win over Celtic on 20 September.

McInnes says the full squad will only train together on Friday, the day before the visit of Kilmarnock and 19 days after their derby triumph.

"Our players are away with different federations, working with different staff and travelling all over the world for four games," McInnes said.

"It's tough for the players to be away from their families, but equally for us there is a lot of nervousness about your players going into other countries' hands for so long.

"They're all back in today but they're not all training. So by the time we get on to the pitch together tomorrow it'll be 19 days since the Celtic game.

"That's longer than a lot of tournaments for a lot of countries. I know it's set in stone - but I'm not a fan of it to be honest."

Shankland sure lots of games to come by return

Why early-season data points to Premiership style shift

Rangers went into the break on a run of six straight victories, the latest two over Celtic in the League Cup and Premiership.

It was a much-needed revival for McInnes, who was named the Premiership manager of the month for September, and his side after a rocky start to his time at Ibrox which involved an exit from European competition.

The Rangers boss says he is under "no illusions" their good form has to continue, and also revealed he had lunch with Sir Alex Ferguson at the club's training ground.

The former Manchester United boss was a regular visitor to Tynecastle last season as McInnes spearheaded Hearts' unexpected title charge.

"He spent a bit of time with the staff and me, chewing the fat as he does," McInnes explained. "He has always been really supportive, and I'm sure he is with a lot of managers.

"I've had a couple of conversations with him since I've been at the club, but to see him in person was good. Particularly after his health scare.

"He enjoyed what we were doing at Hearts and he was a regular visitor. But he understood the opportunity for me to come here was there and we spoke long and hard about that.

"He spoke about his own difficult starts at Man United, and he said it's how you finish a campaign not how you start the campaign. Sometimes it can take time.

"He thought we were really strong on the performance at Celtic Park in particular."

title: College football analyst believes Dabo Swinney has ‘lost his magic’
description: One college football analyst believes Clemson’s Dabo Swinney has lost his magic as a head coach.
fullText:
Clemson's struggles have become impossible to ignore, and one national college football analyst believes the Tigers are facing problems that go well beyond their disappointing start to the season.

Following Clemson's 41-13 loss to No. 4 Miami in Death Valley, CBS Sports columnist Brandon Marcello offered a harsh assessment of where Dabo Swinney's program stands in his Week 5 overreactions column.

Marcello suggested that the Tigers have fallen significantly behind the programs it once competed with for national championships, pointing to an approach that has struggled to keep pace with the changing landscape of college football.

"Clemson has completely lost the magic that transformed it into an annual powerhouse, regressing into a squad trapped in a bygone era."

The loss to Miami, the second-worst defeat of Swinney's tenure, only added to the growing concerns about Clemson's direction. After opening the season with a disappointing performance at LSU, the Tigers have continued to struggle against elite competition.

Marcello also questioned whether Clemson can return to national prominence without major changes to its roster-building strategy.

While Swinney's enormous buyout and legendary status make a coaching change unlikely, Marcello argued that the Tigers must become much more aggressive in the transfer portal. He specifically pointed to the need for a substantial financial commitment, potentially $25 million, to strengthen key positions such as quarterback, wide receiver and the offensive line.

He also raised concerns about Clemson's long-term position in college football, particularly with another round of major television negotiations approaching and the possibility of future conference realignment.

Former Clemson offensive lineman signs contract with Minnesota Vikings

📸 David Jensen, Getty Images https://t.co/KA4ROHLHjv pic.twitter.com/zrqJh8VZdb

For now, Clemson has an opportunity to regroup during its open week before returning to action against Charleston Southern on Oct. 17 at noon on ACC Network.

The Tigers will then resume ACC play against Virginia Tech on Oct. 24 for Homecoming, with kickoff time and television information still to be announced.

fullText:
The 2026 season has been going in favor of the Cleveland Browns and quarterback Deshaun Watson. After being named the organization's starting quarterback, Watson has put together impressive performances, which have ultimately resulted in fewer opportunities for rookie quarterback Shedeur Sanders.

Shedeur Sanders' situation with the Cleveland Browns appears to be moving further away from what the young quarterback may have envisioned when he entered NFL.

In a recent episode of "92.3 The Fan", analysts Jonathan Peterlin and Nick Wilson discussed Sanders' situation in Cleveland and acknowledged how difficult the current circumstances could be for the rookie quarterback.

"I don't know what people think the reaction is going to be from Shador in this moment. I think people think because he's a member of the Browns, he's just supposed to unilaterally cheer for everything that happens Browns related and he's supposed to be excited about everything. Think about it if you're Shador in this spot. You thought going into this year it'd take you two weeks and then you'd be the starter and after week four and starting three and one you realize unless an injury happens you might not start at all this season."

"All right, I think you did fall in line with the strap. It's true, though. I think… What other quarterback do we talk about like that? What other backup quarterback do we say, well, he's going to be disappointed on the sidelines? I think Shador's just not a big reactive guy. But I would say that about any quarterback, though. If you're in their spot and you thought you were going to be able to start this year And it was going to be basically a two-week, let Deshaun Watson fall flat on his face, and then I'll have my opportunity. How are you not disappointed at how this season has gone."

"There's a lot about this year that's gotta be incredibly demoralizing to Shedeur. Individually, this is not going the way that Shedeur Sanders envisioned or wanted."

"What other quarterback do we talk about like that?"

@JPeterlin and @NickWilsonSays on Shedeur Sanders' lack… pic.twitter.com/krqUBBgQ9l

— 92.3 The Fan (@923TheFan) October 6, 2026

With the current situation, it is clear that Sanders is in a difficult position. To continue developing and improving his game, the quarterback needs more practice and game reps. However, with the Browns' starting quarterback performing well, the organization may have little reason to make a change at the position. As a result, Sanders could have to wait longer for an opportunity to gain meaningful experience and prove himself on the field.

At the same time, Sanders will need to remain prepared in case circumstances suddenly change. An injury, a decline in Watson's performance or a change in the coaching staff's plans could give him an opportunity. Until then, his best approach will be to continue improving and proving to the organization that he is ready whenever his opportunity arrives.

The head coach's decision to choose Watson as the starting quarterback is going exactly as he had envisioned. With Watson delivering strong performances and helping the Browns find success, the pathway to the starting role has become longer for Sanders. The rookie quarterback may now have to wait a little longer for his opportunity to prove himself on the field.Fans will be eager to see what the future holds for the rookie quarterback and whether he will eventually get a chance to prove himself on the field.

title: Could the Browns Have Found Useful Backfield Depth in Jaret Patterson?
description: The Cleveland Browns are now providing yet another choice for a running back room that’s already taking some damage in the early going. The Browns have signed Jaret Patterson to the practice squad roster, thereby getting another experienced running back to work alongside until Dylan Sampson is done with his recovery from knee surgery. fullText:
The Cleveland Browns are now providing yet another choice for a running back room that's already taking some damage in the early going.

The Browns have signed Jaret Patterson to the practice squad roster, thereby getting another experienced running back to work alongside until Dylan Sampson is done with his recovery from knee surgery.

Patterson is not arriving with the expectations of becoming the Browns' lead back. The signing seems more about adding another veteran to the fold as the Browns continue to sort through their backfield depth. Patterson has had stints with the Washington Commanders, Los Angeles Chargers, and Minnesota Vikings since his entry into the NFL.

#Browns signed Jaret Patterson to the practice squad. He recently worked out for #Texans

— Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) October 7, 2026

To begin with, the Commanders drafted Patterson from the University of Buffalo in 2021. In 27 NFL games, Patterson rushed for 503 yards with three touchdowns and 126 attempts at the football. In addition to this, he recorded 13 catches for 81 yards. Last year, in six games with the Chargers, Patterson recorded 41 rushes for 159 yards and a touchdown.

It should be noted that the above statistics do not reflect a running back capable of taking control of the backfield, but they do demonstrate that the Browns have at least one player with NFL experience who can replace another injured player. Sampson's absence is the biggest reason for the addition. The Browns have recently been relying more heavily on Raheim Sanders and Jaleel McLaughlin, leaving the team with another reason to keep searching for depth.

Patterson had been with the Vikings in September before being released on September 29. He then worked out for Houston as the Texans explored several potential additions, including Patterson and running back Terrell Jennings. The Browns ultimately won the sweepstakes for his services, at least for now. But there is no shortage of production in Patterson's college résumé either.

His best game ever was against Kent State in November 2020. Patterson rushed for 409 yards and eight touchdowns on 36 carries, setting the record for the most rushing touchdowns in a single game in FBS history. This was followed by his game against Bowling Green when he racked up 301 yards and four touchdowns. Patterson's 710 rushing yards during the two games became the record for the most rushing yards in a two-game period, while his 12 rushing touchdowns did as well.

In total, he had 3,884 rushing yards and 52 touchdowns during his college career with Buffalo. Now he'll need to fight his way onto the Browns' active roster and prove that his experience can be useful as depth behind the Browns' current choices.

The 26-year-old may not be a headline addition, but Cleveland did not need one. It needed another running back, and it found one with NFL experience and a strong college track record.

title: Why Chiefs Star Kenneth Walker Deserves MVP Through First Quarter Of NFL Season
description: Kenneth Walker is the main reason the Chiefs, the only undefeated team in the AFC, has become an explosive offense once again.
fullText:
Last year's Super Bowl MVP could very well become the ensuing season's regular-season MVP.

Through the quarter mark of the season — or what would've been so before the NFL went from 16 games to 17 in 2021 — Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker has been the most valuable player in all of football.

Last year's Chiefs team finished 6-11 and had the 25th-ranked rushing offense.

Now they're the only undefeated team in the AFC and have third best running game in the NFL.

Sure, two-time, regular-season MVP Patrick Mahomes has made a remarkable recovery from reconstructive knee surgery, but last year the Chiefs lacked big-chunk plays in the running game.

During the whole season, running back Kareem Hunt had one 33-yard run, and Isiah Pacheco's longest run was just 16 yards.

In 2026 Walker, the NFL's leading rusher, is one explosive play waiting to happen. He already tops all running backs with six plays of runs of more than 20 yards.

Walker began the season by turning a 4th-and-1 play into a 60-yard touchdown run.

His latest game-changing play came at the end of the third quarter in a game that the Las Vegas Raiders had led for the majority, and it went for 76 yards.

"Man, that's normal for him," Chiefs wide receiver Xavier Worthy said. "We just tell him to take over."

Walker took over the Week Four game when the Chiefs lined up in three-tight-end set. He then ran between the blocks of right guard Trey Smith and right tackle Jaylon Moore. According to Zebra Technologies' analytics, the play was only expected to gain five yards.

Gaining extra yards had been Walker's modus operandi. Not only does he have the speed to outrun defenders, but he also has a knack for breaking their tackles.

He leads the NFL in missed tackles forced this season with 43, and the next highest is Detroit Lions superstar Jahmyr Gibbs, who is 15 behind.

The MVP has basically been a quarterback award of late.

The last running back — and also non-quarterback — to win it was Minnesota Vikings running back Adrian Peterson in 2012.

Peterson rushed for 2,097 in 16 games, and Walker is on pace for 2,282 in 17 games. That would break the single-season mark Eric Dickerson set in the 16-game, 1984 season.

So Walker earning MVP honors would be historic — and valuable in more ways than one.

The last two winners were Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford in 2025 and Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen in 2024. Stafford was in the middle of a two-year, $84 million extension, and Allen was on a six-year, $258 million extension.

Walker would represent a much cheaper alternative as MVP. He is in the first year of a three-year, $43.05 million contract.

And the player with 537 rushing yards does more than run the ball. He has opened up the passing game.

Because of the threat of Walker and the run game, the Chiefs are using the play-action passing game more than ever.

On the very first play of Week Three, a play-action fake to Walker led to Travis Kelce being wide open down the field and to a 48-yard gain — the game's longest play.

A three-down back, Walker already has 84 receiving yards, which is on pace for a career high of 357.

"I could always catch the ball," Walker said. "I just didn't really have opportunities to catch the ball. Coach (Andy) Reid sees that I can catch and make plays in space. So I feel like that's like credit to Coach Reid."

And credit to Chiefs general manager Brett Veach for acquiring Walker in what is shaping up to be the wisest NFL signing this year.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: 'Never feels good': Padres only able to avoid heartbreak for one night
description: The San Diego Padres' postseason run ended with a 3-1 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the NLDS.
fullText:
SAN DIEGO — The San Diego Padres were only able to avoid heartbreak for a single night.

The Padres suffered a 3-1 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers Wednesday, Oct. 7 at Petco Park, ending their postseason.

San Diego's clubhouse was somber, with players reflecting on the season after exchanging handshakes and hugs.

"They are so special," Padres star Fernando Tatis Jr. said about his team after going 1 for 3 with a home run and a walk. "We went through so many ups and downs this year. We became one (after) we went through every battle and just stuck together. It was an enjoyable group to play baseball with."

The Padres showed some fight late in the game with the outcome still in doubt.

All-Star closer Mason Miller avoided disaster in the seventh inning. The Brewers produced a pair of singles and a walk to load the bases before infielder Cooper Pratt lined out to center field, allowing Miller and the Padres to escape the inning.

Miller threw 13 strikes in 21 pitches, allowing two hits while striking out one in the inning.

Manny Machado nearly tied the game in the bottom of the eighth with Tatis on first base, launching a potential two-run home run that was caught at the center-field wall by Garrett Mitchell.

"We had a couple of big pitches and a couple of big swings that didn't quite go our way," Padres general manager A.J. Preller said. "I thought Manny's ball was going out tonight."

Machado also appeared confident that the ball was headed over the fence, dropping his bat and blowing his bubble gum before it was denied by Mitchell at the wall.

It was a déja vú moment for Machado, who had a home run ball robbed by Adam Jones in a memorable World Baseball Classic moment nine years earlier in the same ballpark.

Milwaukee rode starter Robert Gasser and reliever Aaron Ashby for most of the game to help preserve its arms for the NLCS against the Los Angeles Dodgers, who advanced by beating the Atlanta Braves Wednesday.

Ashby finished with three strikeouts while throwing 22 strikes in 38 pitches across three scoreless innings. He replaced Gasser, who pitched the first four innings of the game.

Gasser, a former Padre, allowed three hits and an earned run while striking out three in 56 pitches across four innings.

"You're not going to win it every year," Padres pitcher Joe Musgrove said. "Only one team can win it. … It never feels good (to be eliminated from the playoffs) but I guess as time passes and you gather your thoughts, you can look back at the positives of the season."

title: We have to take emotion out of Saints derby - Adams
description: Pompey midfielder Ebou Adams says there is a fine line between becoming the hero or the villain against Southampton.
fullText:
Portsmouth midfielder Ebou Adams says there is a fine line between becoming the hero or villain in the South Coast derby against rivals Southampton.

Adams netted the equaliser for Pompey against Saints in a 1-1 draw at Fratton Park last season.

And in doing so, the 30-year-old became the first Portsmouth player to score against Southampton since David Norris' 90th-minute equaliser in a 2-2 draw at St Mary's in April 2012.

"The fact that [Norris goal] is still remembered, that shows how important it is," Adams told the Who Needs Mourinho? podcast.

"He scored a last minute equaliser and he's still being spoken about. I've scored an equaliser. What reception would you get if you score a winner?

"If Norris scored 14 years ago and people are still talking about it, it's a chance for someone to be an absolute hero if they score the winner.

"At the same time, when emotion gets into it, you can absolutely become a villain. So we have to be very careful as players."

Pompey visit Southampton on Sunday and Adams said making a costly error in this fixture, such as getting sent off for mistiming a tackle, does not just cost the team - it costs "the whole city".

"You really want to do well for the fans, that's why it's so important to take the emotion out of it as a player because God forbid anyone from either team makes a crazy mistake.

"It can easily be a downward spiral from there because the management of the game is so, so massive."

title: Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion Named First-Team All-Rookies After Fueling Browns’ Surprising Start

fullText:
The Cleveland Browns are getting major returns from their 2026 draft class, and two of their rookie wide receivers are now receiving league-wide recognition for it.

Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion were both named to Dane Brugler's first-team All-Rookie team through four games. The Athletic draft analyst pointed to the pair as major reasons the Browns have opened the season with a surprising 3-1 record.

Brugler did not have to look far when picking the top rookie receivers. Boston has proven to be one of the Browns' most dependable ways of moving the ball down the field, while Concepcion has become yet another critical element of the pass attack.

In four games, Boston has hauled in 13 passes for 284 yards and two touchdowns. Boston's yards per catch mark of 21.8 ranks among the league's best numbers, and he has provided the Browns with an explosive weapon.

"I don't think there is much debate over the top rookie receivers through four games. Boston is one of the best move-the-chain players in the league — 76.9 percent of his catches have resulted in a first down or touchdown, which ranks fifth in the league behind only Mike Evans (88.2 percent), Tee Higgins (80 percent), Jaxon Smith-Njigba (78.1 percent) and Flowers (77.8 percent). He and Concepcion deserve a lot of credit for the Browns' surprising start."

Dane Brugler of The Athletic named Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion to his first-team All-Rookie list, praising their impact on the Browns’ surprising start.

"I don’t think there is much debate over the top rookie receivers through four games. Boston is one of the best… pic.twitter.com/bVTNNlR3pU

— BrownsNation.com (@BrownsNationcom) October 7, 2026

That production has come despite the Browns still working through an evolving quarterback situation. Veteran Deshaun Watson has been the starter, and Boston has already established itself as a target capable of changing a drive with one play.

Concepcion has provided a different kind of impact. The rookie leads the Browns in targets and has seen 17 over the last two games alone. His growing involvement has made the Browns' young receiving group even harder to ignore.

The two rookies are also helping push veteran Jerry Jeudy down the pecking order. Jeudy has only five catches for 62 yards through the first four games, while Boston and Concepcion continue to earn larger roles.

Boston's production has also put him firmly into the Offensive Rookie of the Year conversation. The rookie currently ranks near the top of the rookie class in receiving yards, touchdowns, and yards per reception, while his explosive-play ability has stood out even against veteran receivers.

For the Browns, the bigger story may be how quickly their draft class has translated. Boston and Concepcion are two of four rookies starting on offense, alongside left tackle Spencer Fano and guard Austin Barber. Safety: Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has also made an impact on defense.

Five rookies from the same class earning significant roles this early is unusual; however, Boston and Concepcion are at the center of the attention, and Brugler's first-team selections put another spotlight on just how much the Browns are getting from their young receivers.
