title: Real Madrid already planning reinforcements for two key positions in 2027 – Romano
description: Despite spending a fortune in the transfer market this summer, Real Madrid are looking far from competitive, especially when it comes to keeping up with Barcelona.There are still several weak points t...
fullText:
Despite spending a fortune in the transfer market this summer, Real Madrid are looking far from competitive, especially when it comes to keeping up with Barcelona.

There are still several weak points the club are yet to fix and that is why Los Blancos are already looking towards the season ahead.

The board is expected to continue the spending spree in the summer of 2027, with Fabrizio Romano (h/t Apuesta) revealing two areas they could reinforce.

The Italian journalist suggests Real Madrid's primary objective will be to sign a top defender this season. A centre-back, in particular, is the need of the hour at Real Madrid.

Mourinho has a shortage of centre-backs this season. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images)

Although the club brought in Ibrahima Konate, they also lost David Alaba while Raul Asencio is no longer considered a viable first-team option.

To add to it, Eder MIlitao's fitness woes have continued, with the Brazilian yet to feature this season while Antonio Rudiger could be playing his final season at the club.

This accentuates the need for a new top-class centre-back, which is what Real Madrid will be focusing on next season.

The club have been linked with moves for Alessandro Bastoni and Nico Schlotterbeck, and it won't be surprising to see them being back on Real Madrid's radar for the summer of 2027.

Fumbling Rodri pursuit has come back to haunt Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Another area Real Madrid could look at is the midfield department, with the club still yet to replace the duo of Toni Kroos and Luka Modric.

The team has some proven options in Federico Valverde, Eduardo Camavinga and Aurelien Tchouameni, but they haven't been able to really click or work together in the middle of the park.

Real Madrid require someone who can orchestrate things better. And having missed out on Rodri to Barcelona in the summer, they won't make the same mistake in the summer of 2027.

Romano hasn't exactly spelled out who Real Madrid could target next summer, but there could be multiple options, including past targets such as Kees Smit and Adam Wharton.

title: Zanetti reveals how he went from Inter captain to vice-president
description: Javier Zanetti has revealed how he swapped the training pitch for the boardroom, and why he is still studying to keep up with his role as Inter vice-president.With quotes via CalcioMercato.com, the Ne...
fullText:
Javier Zanetti has revealed how he swapped the training pitch for the boardroom, and why he is still studying to keep up with his role as Inter vice-president.

With quotes via CalcioMercato.com, the Nerazzurri legend was speaking on Melissa Satta's podcast The Long Game, where he also explained the secret behind a physique that looks almost unchanged since his playing days.

"Everyone asks me the secret because I'm the same as I was 30 years ago. Honestly, I live day by day. Everything I do, I do with passion. I always train, every day if I can. When we go on holiday, I joke with my wife: 'Listen, we can go anywhere, you choose. As long as there's a gym.'"

Zanetti made a club-record 858 appearances for Inter between 1995 and 2014, and captained the side to the 2010 Treble. Late in his career he ruptured his Achilles tendon, an injury many expected to end his playing days, but he was back within months and retired a year later.

"I didn't want to end my career that way. I wanted at least one more game in front of my fans at San Siro. It was while I was having a shower that, for the first time, I said to myself: this is my last season. I could have carried on, but I always told myself it's better to stop while you're still doing well."

MILAN, ITALY – MAY 17: Javier Zanetti, Vice President of FC Internazionale Milano, poses for a photo with the Coppa Campioni d'Italia and Coppa Italia trophies following the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and Hellas Verona FC at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on May 17, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

He became vice-president when he retired in 2014, and admits the transition was a steep learning curve.

"I went from training with my teammates on a pitch for 25 years to a meeting of ten managers speaking English about finance and marketing. I started studying, and I'm still studying at Bocconi University. That's the advice I can give young people: don't wait until the end."

Zanetti wants his influence to reach beyond football.

"I want to be an executive who isn't only linked to the sporting side, but who can also be useful for marketing, social causes and all the projects we have to help our club grow. Talent alone isn't enough. Talent needs to be fed every day, you have to train it."

MILAN, ITALY – MAY 17: (L-R) FC Internazionale vice Sportif director Dario Baccin, FC Internazionale Sportif director Piero Ausilio, FC Internazionale President Giuseppe Marotta, FC Internazionale coach Cristian Chivu and FC Internazionale Vice President Javier Zanetti pose for a photo with the Coppa Campioni d'Italia and Coppa Italia trophies following the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and Hellas Verona FC at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on May 17, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

He also called for clubs to pay more attention to players' mental health, an area where Inter already have specialist staff.

"Everyone thinks players are machines: they train, they play and they always have to be at 100 per cent. But it isn't always like that. Many things in a person's private life can affect performance. That's where we have to be careful and work."

title: Did Jerry Jones Just Reveal Agreements Are Already Done for George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr.?
description: Jerry Jones may have accidentally revealed more about the Dallas Cowboys’ plans for George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr. than he intended. Both players are in contract situations that could become major offseason storylines. Pickens is playing on the franchise tag, while Porter Jr. was acquired from the Pittsburgh Steelers in a trade despite being […] The post Did Jerry Jones Just Reveal Agreements Are Already Done for George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr.?
fullText:
Jerry Jones may have accidentally revealed more about the Dallas Cowboys' plans for George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr. than he intended.

Both players are in contract situations that could become major offseason storylines. Pickens is playing on the franchise tag, while Porter Jr. was acquired from the Pittsburgh Steelers in a trade despite being in the final year of his rookie deal. The Cowboys, however, made it sound as if they had already taken care of the business side.

On October 7, Jones was asked about the Cowboys' plans for the two players. His response was notably vague; however, one part immediately stood out. Jones said the Cowboys already have "great agreements" in place concerning Pickens and Porter Jr.

"We don't even have to in any way. We have great agreements. The agreements are in place so that I don't even have to talk about a question like that. I'm not at all perturbed by the question but we've got that put to bed in terms of their business one way or the other. Now, I wouldn't answer as to whether or not we visit about any of their business during the season other than how they're playing or how they're gonna play."

Wow Jerry Jones says there are already agreements in place with George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr: “We don’t even have to in any way. We have great agreements. The agreements are in place so that I don’t even have to talk about a question like that. I’m not at all perturbed by…

— Blitzburgh (@Blitz_Burgh) October 7, 2026

Jones did not clarify whether he was referring to future contracts, existing contractual arrangements, or simply the Cowboys' understanding with both players on how their situations will be handled. Still, the comments are particularly interesting because the Cowboys have already taken a cautious approach with Pickens.

The Cowboys acquired Pickens from the Steelers in 2025 and eventually placed the franchise tag on him after the two sides failed to reach a long-term agreement. He is now playing under a one-year, $27.3M deal, giving the Cowboys another season to evaluate the situation.

There is a similar dilemma with Porter Jr. Dallas traded for the cornerback from Pittsburgh during the season, adding another young player who is approaching the end of his rookie contract. The Cowboys have previously indicated that they were not rushing into an extension, with Porter reportedly focused on proving himself on the field first.

That makes Jones' latest comments even more curious. If the Cowboys truly have an agreement covering the long-term futures of both players, it would remove some significant uncertainty heading into the offseason. The wide receiver is represented by David Mulugheta, and the Cowboys have already acknowledged how difficult it could be to keep him alongside CeeDee Lamb on another massive contract.

However, the cornerback situation is different; the Cowboys also surrendered valuable draft capital to acquire him. For now, though, Jones is not giving away the details.

His comments do suggest that the Cowboys believe the situations with Pickens and Porter Jr. are under control. Whether that means extensions are already agreed upon or simply that the Cowboys have a clear plan for both players remains unclear.

title: Rays troll Yankees by blasting team's victory song in clubhouse during ALDS celebration
description: The Rays were extremely happy to vanquish a division rival.
fullText:
After every victory at home, the New York Yankees blast the "Theme from New York, New York" in the clubhouse. It's become a tradition, one that's stood in place — with some alterations — since the 1980s. The Yankees have done a lot of winning since then.

Unfortunately for the team, traditions are a pretty easy target for tomfoolery when the Yankees lose. The team learned that the hard way Wednesday night, as the Tampa Bay Rays celebrated their American League Division Series sweep over the Yankees by trolling the team with its own victory song.

During the Rays' clubhouse celebration, the team blasted "Theme from New York, New York." Members of the team sang along and started swaying to the music.

#Rays with the local soundtrack pic.twitter.com/F7zKW6bxgP

Rays players clearly delighted in the fact that they were able to eliminate one of their biggest rivals in three straight games. But no player had more fun than Junior Caminero, who mimed sweeping Yankees fans out of the stadium following the contest.

Junior Caminero breaks out the broom for a Rays sweep 🧹 pic.twitter.com/iIPtknS6Rf

Caminero also broke out multiple impressions of former Yankees radio announcer John Sterling's signature call after victories. After every Yankees victory, Sterling would announce, "The Yankees win. Theeeeeeeeeee Yankees win."

Caminero's version changed one key word. You can probably guess which one.

"The Yankees lose!" 😅

Junior Caminero's having a time 🍾 pic.twitter.com/xo9vX4F54U

With the win in the series, the Rays advanced to the American League Championship Series for the third time in franchise history. The team has never lost in the round, advancing to the World Series in each of their previous visits.

The Rays don't know who they'll face in the ALCS just yet. After jumping out to a 2-0 lead in the series, the Chicago White Sox dropped Wednesday's game to the Cleveland Guardians. The White Sox can advance to the ALCS on Thursday with a win over Cleveland. If Chicago loses, both teams will play a winner-take-all Game 5 on Saturday.

title: Hackers hijack Google domains after breaching ccTLD registries
description: Hackers obtained unauthorized HTTPS certificates for several Google domains and hijacked domains in the country-code top-level domains (ccTLDs) for Ghana, American Samoa, and Sierra Leone after compromising third-party operators and modifying authoritative DNS records.
fullText:
Hackers obtained unauthorized HTTPS certificates for several Google domains and hijacked domains in the country-code top-level domains (ccTLDs) for Ghana, American Samoa, and Sierra Leone after compromising third-party operators and modifying authoritative DNS records.

Google underlines that the attacks affected domains of other organizations in the .GH, .SL, and .AS ccTLDs but "did not involve a compromise of Google’s systems."

CAs issue certificates after verifying ownership of the domain, a process that typically requires the requester to create a TXT record with a random value the CA provides.

Modifying the authoritative DNS records allowed the threat actor to point .GH, .SL, and .AS domains to infrastructure they controlled while obtaining valid TLS certificates for those domains.

This let the attacker impersonate legitimate brands and serve visitors arbitrary content from the affected domains.

Google immediately blocked the unauthorized certificates for its properties in Chrome through CRLSets and worked with the issuing authorities to revoke them, extending protection to other clients.

The company said that its systems were not affected by the incident in any way, and that it has no reason to believe that the issuing CAs acted improperly.

After examining Certificate Transparency (CT) logs, the tech giant blocked additional certificates that appeared connected to the attacks and notified affected organizations where possible.

“Following our initial mitigation, Certificate Transparency (CT) log data revealed additional organizations, including several leading global brands and widely used online services, believed to have been impacted by the same attacks,” Google explained.

“To ensure users of those sites were kept safe as soon as possible, we proactively blocked these certificates in Chrome.”

CRLSets is a Chrome “emergency mechanism” designed to allow quick blocking of selected revoked or untrusted HTTPS certificates. Chrome users do not need to take any action to protect themselves from this incident.

However, Google warns that it may not have identified every affected domain, so its current blocking lists might not cover all potential threats.

The tech company also reminded users that CRLSets only covers Chrome users, meaning that users of other browsers might not be protected.

“Due to the complexity of DNS hijacks, we cannot guarantee that our analysis identified every affected domain, nor do Chrome interventions reliably protect non-Chrome users,” Google says.

Certification Authority Authorization (CAA) DNS records cannot stop certificate issuance during an active DNS hijack, but they prevent obtaining additional certificates using cached domain validation after legitimate DNS control is restored, Google notes.

The announcement did not identify the attackers or the quantity of certificates confirmed to have been hijacked.

Join Mikko Hyppönen and security leaders from the NFL, CHANEL, and Atlassian for a two-hour digital summit on what AI-speed attacks change, what defenders should stop doing, and how to validate, decide, fix, and re-validate at machine speed.

title: Experimentguard
description: An A/B test analyzer that tells you whether the results are trustworthy, what broke, and how to fix it. - Balasubramaniyan17/experimentguard
fullText:
Keep your existing experimentation tools. ExperimentGuard tells you whether an A/B test's results are
trustworthy, what broke, and how to reproduce the evidence.

This is the MVP: one workflow. Give it assignment and event data, get a diagnostic report.

Exit codes: 0 trustworthy, 1 suspect, 2 unreliable, 3 bad input. That makes it usable as a CI gate.

Without installing: python -m experimentguard diagnose ...

Exposure events are rows where event_type == "exposure" (change with --exposure-event).
Use --split 90/10 for uneven allocations (sorted-variant order) and --control NAME to pick the baseline.

Every finding includes the numbers, a recommendation, and a SQL query (tables assignments, events)
that reproduces it. All verdicts come from statistical tests; no LLM is involved. An LLM layer for
explaining findings can be added on top, but it should only narrate the evidence, never decide validity.

title: Trump Tourism Effects
description:
In the past day or two on social media I kept seeing this graph from a Semafor story on the declining volume of international visitors to the United States.
Semafor Graph.
It seems to show, and was being remarked on as showing, that the second Trump administration has been responsible for a drop in visitors from abroad from some countries on a scale comparable to the effects of the Covid-19 pandemic. My first thought was “that can’t be true”. And indeed it is not true.
fullText:
In the past day or two on social media I kept seeing this graph from a Semafor story on the declining volume of international visitors to the United States.

It seems to show, and was being remarked on as showing, that the second Trump administration has been responsible for a drop in visitors from abroad from some countries on a scale comparable to the effects of the Covid-19 pandemic. My first thought was “that can’t be true”. And indeed it is not true. I mean, the pandemic shut down air travel almost completely for a while. The current administration’s actions have been terrible in many ways and led to direct, negative consequences for tourism, too. But they haven’t been on that scale. Something’s wrong with the graph.

These numbers come from International Trade Administration’s I-94 arrivals data. They maintain a spreadsheet that counts all international visitors by country of residence who arrive in the U.S., spend at least one night here, are among qualified visa holders, including tourist visas and waivers and so forth. This is a monthly series. Right now, we only have data up to August of 2026, and for a couple of countries in the graph only up till June. I think—I am only guessing—that what the person who made this graph did was aggregate to yearly totals, plot those points, and then smooth them. (That’s why the y-axis values are so large in comparison to the ones on the monthly graphs I’m about to show you.) But the data for 2026 are only for half the year, hence the giant drop.

I went and got the data myself and took a look at it. Here’s the raw monthly series for the same countries as in the one above:

It’s noisy because tourism is highly seasonal. Even so, the catastrophic effects of the pandemic are obvious, as is the fact that whatever is going on in the past year isn’t nearly as severe as that. Though something is going on. We can smooth the monthly data directly by calculating a trailing average, which is just a moving average except the window we’re moving across the data doesn’t extend beyond the current month. That way, we don’t illegitimately “look ahead” of the current month in a way that would make our moving average seem to anticipate the future. If we used an ordinary moving average it might seem like the trend was able to anticipate the Covid-19 downturn, for example. Here’s the result:

So, no Covid-scale drop. But still, not nothing. The Canadian dip, following the trade war Trump started for no good reason, is very substantial. Just eyeballing it, it seems about twice as large as the downturn that followed the global financial crisis of the Great Recession, which is quite remarkable. It also looks like French tourism has declined, but I’d need to look a little more closely at that series by itself, as it’s on quite a different scale.

The general lesson, I suppose, is just that it’s always worth trying to cultivate some sort of rough comparative sense of how big or small an effect you should be expecting to see in your data, so that when something goes wrong (as things so often do) you’re more likely to be brought up short by it.

Speaking of which, you might also wonder about the remarkable leap in visitors from Mexico around 2004-2005 that’s visible in both the original graph and my version of it. What happened there? The answer is not some sudden shift in tourism preferences, but our old friend, measurement change. Prior to 2005, visitors from Mexico originating within 25 miles of the border weren’t counted as visitors. After 2005, they were. Hence the jump. In a smaller but still noticeable way, data for 2014 aren’t fully comparable either, because overseas one-night-stay visitors were included that year. There is some documentation of this on this old BTS page. If you want to measure change, you can’t change the measure.

Update: Now that I have this data and am messing around with it, here’s one more. This is monthly data averaged with a 12-month trailing window, showing all travel to the U.S., broken out by different “regions”. Canada and Mexico are large enough to each be their own region. Looking at things this way deliberately smooths away all the seasonality. The size of the Canadian reaction to the Trump administration’s attack on them really is remarkable. Elbows up, Canada.

title: I gave Opus 5.5 one prompt and six hours to visualize Invisible Cities
description: Claude Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6 Astra one-shot Invisible Cities by Italo Calvino in Three.js: AI design, UX, data visualization and explorable explanations.
fullText:
GPT-6 Astra was a jump when it comes to puzzles.
Claude Opus 5.5 is a jump when it comes to design.

Even local models can make a competent landing page for a shop. Doing interactive visualization is a different tier. Since I am into creating data visualizations and explorable explanations, LLMs were both a blessing and a curse.

Then for a moment I was happy-ish with GPT-6 Astra. My subjective experience was that it is a bit better than Fable 5.1 at a general overview, following intentions behind prompts, and checking that it all works correctly.

Then there was the Opus 5.5 moment for AI-assisted design. I saw an optical explorable explanation:

One may argue that it is still “too rich”, and has no sense of minimalism. But still, wow!
I was still in disbelief. Was this really its consistent quality for a one-shot experiment?

Instead of my beloved optics, I went for something different.

What’s a good prompt? Well, I went with the beautiful urbanistic poetry of Invisible Cities by Italo Calvino, presenting 55 imaginative cities, each one an emotion or state of mind, expressed in its architecture and in how people behave.

When a man rides a long time through wild regions he feels the desire for a city. Finally he comes to Isidora, a city where the buildings have spiral staircases encrusted with spiral seashells, where perfect telescopes and violins are made, where the foreigner hesitating between two women always encounters a third, where cockfights degenerate into bloody brawls among the bettors.

In 2019, I had a small project of generating cities for a storytelling performance, using the frontier model of the time, GPT-2. With new models, capabilities change drastically. So I used the following prompt:

Make a three.js (pnpm) visualization of all Invisible Cities by Italo Calvino. Don’t ask questions, it is a one-shot task. You have 6h of work, use it until it becomes a masterpiece.

I gave this prompt to GPT-6 Astra… and it worked, end-to-end.

Some AI design slop, with many concepts and comments added, without checking whether they are actually needed, or just add visual noise. Some Captain Obvious statements that would work for accessibility, but not as something to be shown verbatim.

Curiously, it seemed to pick up the Claude visualization style: beige background, numbers like 05.
Still, I wouldn’t have expected earlier models to get anywhere near this.

Then I gave the same prompt to Claude Opus 5.5. It claimed:

I used roughly half of the six hours. The remaining polish has diminishing returns, but I can do another round if you want.

In fact it used only 1 hour 25 minutes, despite my direct instruction; though you can argue that it used agentic time dilation: 6 subagents, running in parallel, added up to about 7 agent-hours. I wanted to scold Opus 5.5 for finishing early, but then peeked at the result.

And I’m mesmerized! See it for yourself.
Sure, it might (and should) have used all the time, but even at this stage it was “wow!”.
If this is the actual ceiling, it is a high one. And I am sure the next models will go even higher.

I encourage you to use the same prompt with different models, or different harnesses.

We can expect AI to be a tool widely used (and burning a lot of token budget) in design.

I’m in awe, but I’m also asking myself: what is my place in creating interactive media?

title: Sony Sells Patents to Meta, Seemingly Signifies End of VR Efforts
description: PSVR2, we barely knew ye.
fullText:
It's no secret that Sony's PlayStation VR2 headset hasn't quite seen the support that VR fans might have expected, with relatively few high profile games after the system's initially promising launch back in 2023 - we called it a "state of the art experience" in our review. Now, the company looks like it may be stepping back from VR and related XR/AR development in a big way, as it has sold 43 US patents to rivals Meta.

The news, which was first reported by ZDNet Korea, shows that the sale took place between June and September, with patents ranging from those relating to specific types of XR glasses, head-mounted displays and related software. In total, 419 patents will be transferred from Sony to Meta, with 180 patents in the US and the remainder in Europe, Asia and other regions.

Thus far, we've only seen one flagship release from Sony from the headset - Horizon: Call of the Mountain - and I only really see this game and Gran Turismo 7's VR mode being mentioned online or in conversations with friends. Sony did follow up the PS5 release with a PC adapter that let the headset work with a much wider range of VR titles, but other PS VR2 specific releases have been extremely thin on the ground.

In fact, the "upcoming PS VR2 games" section on the PS Store doesn't include anything on the brink of release. Thief VR: Legacy of Shadow is the biggest name but came out in 2025, "Shadowgate VR: The Mines of Mythrock" [sic] is misspelled and also came out in 2025, and Out of Sight VR still lacks a release date despite reportedly coming out by the end of 2026 - its Steam release has been abandoned for 18 months. It's clear that the PS Store page hasn't been updated in at least a year.

Did you pick up a PSVR2? Are you happy with how it's been supported? Let me know in the comments below. For more VR discussion, why not read our interview with Valve about the Steam Frame?

title: Parents in Finland turn to AI for free school pictures
description: Some parents are using AI tools to strip watermarks from their kids' school photos.
fullText:
It's that time of year again: the school semester is underway, and many kids have already had their annual photo day.

But this year, there's a twist. Some parents in Finland are feeding preview images of their kids' portraits into AI tools to wipe away the copyright text.

As some families debate the issue on social media, the Finnish school photographers' association said it has learned of isolated cases where photos have been used without permission.

That means the photographer does not get paid for their work.

According to the association's vice chair, Outi Simström, there is a common misunderstanding about the sector's earnings model.

"A photographer is not paid by the school or daycare for coming in and photographing the children. The entrepreneur's income comes from families voluntarily buying the pictures they want," Simström said.

As a general rule, photographs may not be copied or published without the photographer's permission. If a photograph qualifies as a copyright-protected work, the protection lasts considerably longer.

Simström also warns parents about the risks of using AI.

"When we're talking about a picture of a person, and especially a minor, it's material and personal data of a kind that I would always recommend thinking carefully about which external digital service you upload these images to. Afterwards, they can't easily be removed."

Using photographs without permission is hardly a new phenomenon, according to Mikko Säteri of Finnfoto, the umbrella organisation for Finland's photography associations.

For around a decade, parents have captured pictures by removing watermarks with various tools and software. AI, however, has added a new dimension to the practice.

"AI can enlarge an image file enough to make a printable copy from it," he explained.

Säteri said photography businesses are now having to develop new ways to protect their images and track down those used without permission.

School photography is a Finnish tradition going back 160 years. But Säteri said he is now concerned about whether these businesses can survive in the age of AI.

School snaps feature prominently in Säteri's own home, as they do in many others.

"I think it's wonderful to see photographs of my daughters from different periods lined up on the fridge."

title: Building an Internal Company Agent: Things We Got Right, 5 I'd Do Differently
description: A practical retrospective on building and rolling out an internal company agent at Bold.org, from connectors and usage analytics to adoption, contributions and overbuilt evals.
fullText:
In my recent AI engineering setup article, I briefly explained how an observability project at Bold.org turned into an internal company agent.

The short version is that back in January 2026, Bold.org had structured backend events in ClickHouse, engineers could investigate them with SQL, and I wanted to see whether an agent could do the same. It worked, so I kept connecting more company systems. Within weeks, people across Bold.org were using it. It eventually became useful across engineering, product, support, operations, marketing, and growth.

That summary makes the path sound much cleaner than it was.

Several decisions helped the agent spread quickly. I also spent time solving problems I did not really have, left some important problems too late, and assumed things were obvious when they definitely were not.

This is not a universal guide to building agents. It is a practical retrospective from building one inside a real company: five things we got right and five I would approach differently today.

The first workflow was straightforward: I gave the agent read-only access to structured backend events in ClickHouse so it could investigate production questions. I then connected more of the systems where people already worked, including Slack, Linear, PostHog, and Grafana.

The practical effect is bigger than a faster way to write SQL. Support can investigate many customer reports autonomously, without waiting for engineering or another team to provide context. For the workflows we target, investigations that previously took multiple hours and required finding the right access through three or four people can usually be completed in zero to one hour. The agent also automates parts of dashboard setup and analysis in PostHog and Grafana without requiring engineering to step in.

The system consumes billions of tokens per month. That makes usage analytics and cost awareness important, but it is also a useful signal that the tool is part of how people work rather than a demo that is occasionally opened.

I made one security boundary deliberately simple. The agent is gated behind Google sign-in for our company domain, and all of its remote access is read-only. Rather than relying on the model to be smart about when a change is safe, I did not give it permissions to write to remote systems in the first place.

It is tempting to build an internal tool privately, make it feel complete, write an announcement, and then ask everyone to use it. We did almost the opposite. The agent was used in shared Slack channels and connected to Linear, where people were already working and could see what it did.

This mattered more than any launch document.

Most people do not immediately know what an agent can do. A blank chat box does not explain its capabilities. Even a good list of examples still requires someone to translate those examples into their own work.

Seeing real usage solves that problem. Someone asks a question in Slack, the agent investigates it, and ten other people see both the result and the way the question was asked. A product manager notices that it can inspect a user flow. Somebody in support realizes it can help investigate a report. An engineer sees it gather context they were about to collect manually.

Each visible interaction becomes a small product demo based on an actual company problem.

Slack and Linear were important for another reason: they did not require people to adopt a new destination. Another internal web application would have asked everyone to remember that the tool existed, open it, and decide when to use it. In Slack and Linear, the agent appears where the question or task already exists.

The web interface is still useful, especially for private or longer work. But shared usage is what taught the company what was possible.

When I started this in January, MCP was still emerging and many of the systems we needed did not have useful servers. I closed the gap with small CLI tools, mostly thin wrappers around OpenAPI endpoints or existing SDKs, exposing only the operations needed for our workflows. They were intentionally boring: structured results, narrow permissions, proper error handling, and credentials kept away from the model.

The value was not just another action the agent could take. More access meant more company context: production data, tickets, analytics, dashboards, and operational information could be considered together. That gave the agent better evidence for its reasoning and made its answers more useful than anything it could infer from a single system.

Usage analytics went in early. Not to create a leaderboard or measure who was “doing AI” correctly, but to understand what had been built.

Tool calls, token spend, recurring workflows, and broad usage patterns showed which tools were valuable, where requests were becoming expensive, and what capabilities people kept trying to use. That made it possible to improve the product based on behavior rather than guesses: unexpected usage suggested a workflow needed simplifying, while unused tools pointed to poor discoverability, descriptions, or limited value. Aggregate operational metrics were more useful than ranking individuals and kept the analytics focused on improving the tool rather than monitoring employees.

People will try things you did not anticipate. They will also hit confusing behavior that feels obvious to the person who built the system.

Feedback was easy to share, and the agent was adjusted as people used it. This sounds basic, but it created a useful loop: somebody tried a workflow, reported where it failed, and could often try the improved version shortly afterwards.

That responsiveness encouraged more experimentation. People are much more willing to explore a new tool when they know a failure is not the end of the conversation.

Some basic documentation also helped. It did not need to explain every tool or become a complete AI training course. A short explanation of what the agent could access, examples of good requests, known limitations, and how to share feedback gave people enough confidence to start.

The combination matters. Documentation without feedback becomes stale. Feedback without documentation means answering the same introductory questions forever.

The agent started from an engineering and observability problem, so keeping it focused on engineers would have been the obvious path. That would have been a mistake.

Some of the most interesting usage came from product, support, operations, marketing, and growth. These teams often need information spread across several systems but do not have a convenient way to query or combine it. An agent with the right company context can remove a lot of that navigation. Support can be especially powerful here: people can investigate many reports themselves instead of waiting for engineering to gather the context.

Engineers can actually be harder to convince.

They already have coding agents, terminal workflows, preferred models, custom instructions, and strong opinions about harnesses. Asking them to move into a shared company interface can feel like asking them to give up a setup they spent months refining. I understand the resistance because I have the same opinions about my own tools.

Other departments may have fewer existing agent workflows to replace. Once they see a relevant example and trust the access model, the value can be more immediate.

Treating the agent as company infrastructure rather than an engineering experiment changed both its adoption and the features that mattered most.

The biggest missing piece is making company tools available safely from local agent harnesses.

The shared web, Slack, and Linear interfaces are useful, but local agents have context that a company agent does not. They can work with a person’s files, notes, project memory, terminal, and current repository. Engineers in particular do not want to abandon that context every time they need company information.

The ideal setup is not forcing everyone into one harness. It is allowing approved local harnesses to use company tools without exposing credentials or bypassing permissions.

That is a much harder problem than adding another interface. Authentication needs to represent the person making the request. Secrets cannot be handed to the local model. Tool access should remain scoped and auditable. A compromised or badly configured local environment should not gain broad company access.

Agent tooling changes constantly. Frameworks appear, models improve, MCP conventions evolve, and every week there is a new opinion about what AI should be, how it should be built, and which patterns or use cases are right or wrong.

It is very easy to keep redesigning the system around what everyone is discussing online.

I spent too much time considering whether I should rebuild parts of the agent around the latest approach. Most of that thinking had a short expiry date: a tool or pattern that looked essential one month could be irrelevant a few months later. Today I would pick one simple architecture that supports the immediate use case and move forward. Keep connectors small, keep boundaries clear, avoid coupling everything to one model or framework, and replace pieces only when there is a real reason rather than because a new diagram is popular on social media.

Internal tools have an advantage here: they do not need to become a generic platform for every possible customer. They need to solve the company’s actual problems.

The agent improved quickly, but too much of that improvement depended on a small number of people.

It was not obvious who could write a skill, add a connector, improve instructions, or contribute code. Even when the repository was available, people were understandably hesitant. Agent systems combine code, prompts, permissions, and unfamiliar conventions. Nobody wants to break a tool used across the company or accidentally expose something sensitive.

I have not solved this yet. People are welcome to use the agent, but it is not obvious how to contribute safely. The repository is available, but writing a skill, adding a connector, or changing instructions requires understanding code, prompts, permissions, and unfamiliar conventions.

A short contribution guide with examples, ownership, review requirements, and a safe test path would make this easier. Until then, too much of the improvement depends on a small number of people.

I spent too much time on evals, detailed traces, and comparing model behavior. Some visibility is essential: enough tracing to debug failures, usage analytics to control spend, and tests for critical tools and permissions. But this is not a frontier lab or a product with a dedicated evaluation team. It is an internal tool, and I cannot devote all my time to building infrastructure around hypothetical failures.

The goal is to make it simple, make it work, and keep it maintainable. A few representative workflows and permission tests are enough until recurring failures justify more. The evaluation system should grow from real problems rather than from the fear of not measuring enough.

The largest mistake was probably assuming that capabilities obvious to me would be obvious to everyone else.

AI adoption varies enormously across departments and individuals. Some people work with agents all day. Others have only used the basic ChatGPT interface. Terms such as tools, memory, connectors, context, or skills may mean nothing to them, and there is no reason they should.

From the builder’s perspective, the benefit seems clear: the agent can search several company systems, combine what it finds, and act on the result. From somebody else’s perspective, it may look like another chat box. Why use this instead of ChatGPT? What does it know? What can it do? What is safe to ask? Will it make a change without permission?

I have not solved this completely either.

What helps most is turning abstract capabilities into visible functionality. Do not announce that the agent has a new connector. Show that it can prepare a specific report, investigate a known type of issue, or automate a repetitive workflow. Give people something relevant they can try immediately.

Adoption does not happen because the architecture is impressive. It happens when somebody sees the agent solve a problem they recognize.

These are the main lessons and mistakes from the first six months: make the agent visible early, connect it to the systems where context lives, keep access safe, and optimize for something simple enough to maintain.

The best decision was letting people see the agent being used before it felt finished. The recurring lesson is that what feels obvious to the builder is rarely obvious to everyone else.

I am interested in hearing how other teams are adopting AI in practice, what is working, and where workflows are still awkward or blocked by access, context, or trust. If you are working through similar questions or facing challenges introducing AI-native workflows in your team or company, I would love to hear more and see whether I can help.

title: Flight attendants warn Trump's Washington arch could threaten airport safety
description:
— The union representing thousands of flight attendants said Wednesday it has safety concerns about President Donald Trump's proposed triumphal arch that will be on final approach to Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.
Association of Flight Attendants-CWA President Sara Nelson said the 250-foot (76 meter) arch compounds multiple safety concerns that she said have gone unaddressed from a deadly January 2025 crash over the Potomac River that killed 67 people. Nelson also criticized Trump's plan to turn the arch into "a top grade military complex” able to host drones and snipers while storing ammunition.
“DCA is already stretched to its limit, we do not need an obstacle taking up space in our flight path,” said Nelson. “Nor should commercial aviation have to dodge military drones, missiles or snipers while attempting to take off or land at Washington National Airport.
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The union representing thousands of flight attendants said Wednesday it has safety concerns about President Donald Trump's proposed triumphal arch that will be on final approach to Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.

Association of Flight Attendants-CWA President Sara Nelson said the 250-foot (76 meter) arch compounds multiple safety concerns that she said have gone unaddressed from a deadly January 2025 crash over the Potomac River that killed 67 people. Nelson also criticized Trump's plan to turn the arch into "a top grade military complex" able to host drones and snipers while storing ammunition.

"DCA is already stretched to its limit, we do not need an obstacle taking up space in our flight path," said Nelson. "Nor should commercial aviation have to dodge military drones, missiles or snipers while attempting to take off or land at Washington National Airport. Safety first always."

Nelson's statement on behalf of the union, which represents 55,000 flight attendants across 20 airlines, joins the voices of an assemblage of veterans' groups, Congress members and others with safety concerns and complaints about the memorial's threat to historic and symbolic sightlines between different landmarks in Washington, D.C.

Though the arch has received early approval from the U.S. Commission of Fine Arts, whose members were all tapped by Trump, a group of three veterans and an architectural historian sued, saying the project needs to be approved by Congress.

Last month, the Republican president said in a social media post that he had agreed, at the "strong request" of the military, to convert the planned 250-foot-tall (76-meter) memorial arch "into a top grade Military Complex."

The Federal Aviation Administration said last month before Trump's announcement on it becoming a military complex that the arch would not pose a hazard to aircraft, but it should be "appropriately marked with a non-standard eternal flame on top of the structure and floodlight projectors pointed towards the arch to make it noticeable for pilots.

An assessment by the National Park Service said the memorial arch could disrupt the historical significance of dozens of nearby sites. The Park Service approved the project despite its assessment.

Interior Secretary Doug Burgum announced early last month that excavation work on the site in Memorial Circle would begin within weeks. The Interior Department did not respond immediately to questions on the status of that work.

The arch is one of several projects around Washington that Trump has undertaken as he remakes the city, from renovating one of its storied public golf courses to threatening to demolish the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts.

This story has been updated to correct the union's name. It is the Association of Flight Attendants-CWA , not Flight Attendants Association-CWA.

title: Cornell rape accuser was told police were still investigating. They weren't, her lawyer says.
description:
ITHACA, N.Y. (AP) — The woman accusing several men of raping her at a Cornell University fraternity party was “misled” about the status of the criminal investigation in the weeks after she went to police, her lawyer said Wednesday.
Even as she took her allegations about a 2024 gang rape at the Chi Phi fraternity house through Cornell's internal disciplinary process, the university's police department gave her the impression that a criminal investigation was continuing, lawyer Thomas Giuffra told The Associated Press.
In fact, the criminal inquiry ended almost as soon as it began.
fullText:
ITHACA, N.Y. (AP) — The woman accusing several men of raping her at a Cornell University fraternity party was "misled" about the status of the criminal investigation in the weeks after she went to police, her lawyer said Wednesday.

Even as she took her allegations about a 2024 gang rape at the Chi Phi fraternity house through Cornell's internal disciplinary process, the university's police department gave her the impression that a criminal investigation was continuing, lawyer Thomas Giuffra told The Associated Press.

In fact, the criminal inquiry ended almost as soon as it began.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, the local prosecutor, made the decision not to go forward with a criminal case within days of the woman giving her first substantial interviews to police.

Van Houten has said that he asked Cornell's police department to convey the decision to the woman, who is referred to in court documents as Jane Doe, but never spoke personally to her or her lawyer.

Giuffra said the woman was told that the criminal investigation was ongoing.

"I think she was misled. She was told it was still — they weren't going to prosecute, but they were still investigating," Giuffra said. "I was involved with this case early on. I thought they were still investigating. It was news to me that they weren't doing anything."

Giuffra added that at the time, he assumed investigators just needed more time to speak with witnesses and build a case.

"But nothing was being done, and we didn't know that," Giuffra said.

A message seeking comment was left for Van Houten. Cornell's media relations office, citing pending litigation, declined to comment on behalf of the university's police department.

The district attorney said in a statement last week that he was confident that no further investigation was necessary after prosecutors and criminal investigators from his office reviewed a six-page summary of the woman's account, written by a police officer.

Based on that summary, Van Houten said he believed no crime had been committed, and that the woman's participation in drug use and sex was "voluntary, conscious and consensual."

That description differs sharply with what the woman told police and university investigators, and with what she alleged in a lawsuit filed against seven Chi Phi fraternity members, Cornell and others last month.

Among other things, Giuffra said, the six-page report omitted the woman telling investigators, "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped," that she was subjected to physical violence, and that a fraternity brother had sent a message to a group chat using a vulgar term to advertise that a woman's body was freely available.

Last week, citing investigative records it obtained, The New York Times reported that a Cornell police investigator tried to get Van Houten's office to consider additional evidence in the weeks after the alleged rape, but was rebuffed.

"At first I thought these police were incompetent," Giuffra said. "It sounds like they were doing the right thing. And they just got shut down."

Giuffra said that while he and Jane Doe have received death threats, he has been heartened by an outpouring of support, including rallies and protests on the Cornell campus and more than 1,000 women who have emailed him to share anger, frustration, solidarity and stories of their own assaults.

Some Cornell students staged a sit-in at a dining hall and vowed not to spend money on campus Wednesday to protest sexual violence and how the university has handled complaints, in the latest expression of outrage over an alleged 2024 gang rape at a fraternity house.

A handwritten sign reading "Justice for Jane Doe " — the name under which the accuser is suing — was propped on an empty table in the dining hall in the afternoon. Some students sat around the room without eating, while others lunched. Another small group sat outside holding signs with messages such as "we are Jane Doe."

The demonstrations were meant to spotlight complaints that the university is slow to respond to reports of sexual assault while quick to protect its reputation. Among other demands, the groups want the university to retool disciplinary procedures for addressing complaints and expel or revoke the degrees of anyone involved in the alleged October 2024 sexual assault.

Jane Doe, who was a student then, alleges that Chi Phi members plied her with alcohol and drugs and several sexually assaulted her. One man sent others a message inviting them to participate, according to a lawsuit she filed last month.

Lawyers for two of the men have denied they participated in a sexual assault. Attempts by The Associated Press to reach the others or their representatives have been unsuccessful. Some of the men who underwent a university disciplinary hearing in 2024 told investigators that the sexual activity was consensual or said they were not involved.

The woman went to Cornell police in November 2024, though no criminal charges resulted. In the wake of her lawsuit, Van Houten said he was reopening the investigation. Days later, Gov. Kathy Hochul took the case away from him and appointed the state's attorney general, Letitia James, as a special prosecutor.

Giuffra applauded the move, saying he was troubled by Van Houten's plan for conducting the reopened investigation and "didn't think he was up to the task." Giuffra said the district attorney wanted to take the case to a grand jury and have Jane Doe testify before the panel within two weeks.

That timeline, leaving little time to review evidence or interview witnesses, suggested that Van Houten may have been trying "to go take a dive and not really give it his best effort and not do any investigation," Giuffra said.

James hasn't said how long her investigation might take, but she suggested it would take months.

On Wednesday, one of the men named in Jane Doe's lawsuit filed a court petition seeking James' removal from the case, arguing she showed bias by posting on social media a few days before her appointment: "What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable."

A spokesperson for James declined to comment.

Cornell closed down the Chi Phi campus chapter in 2024 and says it expelled some students and suspended others after an investigation under the federal Title IX law.

This week Cornell trustees brought in former U.S. Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates to review how the school investigates sexual assault and sexual harassment, how the disciplinary process works, the campus police response and more.

title: University of Arizona suspends all fraternity activities as misconduct reports pile up
description:
TUCSON, Ariz. (AP) — The University of Arizona has suspended activities at its fraternities following persistent reports of misconduct, including assault, hazing, and drug and alcohol-related behavior, a university official said.
Just seven weeks into the fall semester, the university's Dean of Students Office was investigating multiple misconduct reports involving nearly half the school's Interfraternity Council chapters, Dean Chrissy Lieberman said Monday in a letter to the school's fraternities and sororities announcing the suspension.
The reports follow misconduct findings against some interfraternity chapters in the spring and multiple criminal investigations, according to the letter.
“The number of cases under investigation and the severity of the concerns is egregious,” Lieberman wrote.
fullText:
TUCSON, Ariz. (AP) — The University of Arizona has suspended activities at its fraternities following persistent reports of misconduct, including assault, hazing, and drug and alcohol-related behavior, a university official said.

Just seven weeks into the fall semester, the university's Dean of Students Office was investigating multiple misconduct reports involving nearly half the school's Interfraternity Council chapters, Dean Chrissy Lieberman said Monday in a letter to the school's fraternities and sororities announcing the suspension.

The reports follow misconduct findings against some interfraternity chapters in the spring and multiple criminal investigations, according to the letter.

"The number of cases under investigation and the severity of the concerns is egregious," Lieberman wrote.

University spokesman Nick Prevenas did not immediately respond to a request 

The Associated Press left messages with the university's police agency. Officer Frank Magos, a spokesperson for the Tucson Police Department, said he was unaware of recent cases involving fraternities that were investigated by the city's police agency.

Prevenas also did not say whether the suspension was triggered by recent public outcry over how Cornell University handled allegations that multiple fraternity brothers sexually assaulted a woman in 2024. Lieberman's letter noted that "the value of the Greek experience is under scrutiny nationwide."

The suspension prohibits fraternities from hosting, attending, participating in and sponsoring any organizational activities at least until their advisers have met with Lieberman at one of three meetings that were scheduled for Tuesday, Wednesday and Oct. 12, according to the letter.

The letter said the dean's office had reached "capacity" to investigate misconduct reports, and that reports continued even after the university's president warned Interfraternity Council presidents at an August meeting about the possibility of additional consequences.

"It is time for the University of Arizona Greek community to step up and set an example for good," the letter said. "It is time to have difficult conversations with each other and the members of the community."

The university had previously suspended activities at the Sigma Tau Gamma fraternity after new members last year were reportedly forced to consume large quantities of alcohol and live goldfish and were subjected to screaming, degradation, and threats, according to a Sept. 2 letter from a university official to the fraternity.

An email and phone message at the fraternity's national headquarters were not immediately returned. The AP also reached out to six other fraternity chapters at the University of Arizona's campus via social media seeking comment on the suspensions.

title: ISIS-inspired mass shooting plot at Mall of America thwarted, FBI says
description:
Federal authorities have arrested a man accused of planning to carry out an ISIS-inspired mass shooting at the Mall of America in Minnesota, according to newly unsealed court records. 
Sheikhdoon Mohamud was taken into custody Tuesday after allegedly purchasing an AK-47 and 200 rounds of ammunition from a confidential source for the FBI that prosecutors say he planned to use to attack a festival taking place at the Mall of America. 
Mohamud has been under investigation by the FBI since December 2024 when a confidential source with the FBI began exchanging messages with him about either traveling to Somalia to fight on behalf of al-Shabaab or carrying out a mass casualty attack on U.S. soil, court documents show.
fullText:
The FBI arrested an 18-year-old for allegedly planning a mass casualty attack.

Federal authorities have arrested a man accused of planning to carry out an ISIS-inspired mass shooting at the Mall of America in Minnesota, according to newly unsealed court records.

Sheikhdoon Mohamud was taken into custody Tuesday after allegedly purchasing an AK-47 and 200 rounds of ammunition from a confidential source for the FBI that prosecutors say he planned to use to attack a festival taking place at the Mall of America.

Mohamud has been under investigation by the FBI since December 2024 when a confidential source with the FBI began exchanging messages with him about either traveling to Somalia to fight on behalf of al-Shabaab or carrying out a mass casualty attack on U.S. soil, court documents show.

Prosecutors detail scores of communications between Mohamud and the FBI source where he allegedly detailed his hopes of martyrdom, including one where he discussed just getting a "gun here and just start killing a bunch of white ppl."

Prosecutors said Mohamud told the source he wanted to attack the Mall of America "because its owned by jewish" people, adding, "so if I kill even 30 people noone would go there anymore."

Mohamud later allegedly settled on a meetup of Oct. 6 with the source to purchase the weapons and suggested he would plan to carry an attack on Oct. 24 targeting the Hmong Arts Celebration at the Mall of America, according to court documents.

During their meetup the undercover agent handed Mohamud a large duffel bag containing an AK-47 rifle and four magazines as well as a container with 200 rounds of ammunition, according to prosecutors.

The agent told Mohamud he was a member of ISIS and when he asked him about his attack plans, Mohamud again allegedly expressed intent to carry out a shooting at a festival at the Mall, and said part of his motivation was that he believed it was owned by Jews and that he was "angry at the bad treatment of Muslims" in the wake of the May attack on an Islamic Center in San Diego.

Upon exiting the vehicle, Mohamud was taken into custody at gunpoint by FBI agents, the affidavit says.

"The American people and the citizens of Minnesota should know from yesterday's arrest -- which was the culmination of an outstanding law enforcement and intelligence operation -- that federal law enforcement is standing up to their calling to protect us," U.S. attorney for Minnesota Dan Rosen said Wednesday. "Here, because of their vigilance and diligence, they were able to detect the threat and disrupt it before the defendant carried out his intention to kill, in his words, 'maybe 30 to 60 people,' as we allege in far greater detail in the complaint."

Rosen and FBI special agent Christopher Dodson detailed the extensive communications between Mohamud and an FBI confidential source that they said showed he was "100% committed" to carrying out an attack.

"The messages this defendant allegedly sent to others were chilling," Dodson said. "They show the idolization of ideologically motivated violence, a callous disregard for the sanctity of human life, a blind hatred of people of other faiths, and a cold commitment to carrying out his vision of violence in our community."

Mohamud is believed to be an American citizen born in the United States, Rosen told reporters, though in the criminal complaint he refers to Somalia as the homeland of his parents.

Rosen noted that in 2025 after being alerted to his sharing of extremist material online, the FBI actually went to Mohamud's house to attempt to speak to his parents but were rebuffed.

"I just would say to parents all over Minnesota -- for that matter, all over America: If you get the indication, especially if you hear from federal law enforcement that your son or daughter is being radicalized to the point where federal law law enforcement wants to come and give you that warning, those are warnings that ought to be heeded," Rosen said.

title: Russian strike on buses kills 30 people in frontline Ukrainian city
description:
Police said the buses were hit with a glide bomb (Handout)
Ukraine on Thursday accused Russia of deliberately targeting civilians after 30 people were killed when two buses were blown up in the frontline city of Kramatorsk, in one of the deadliest single attacks for weeks.
Photos posted by local authorities showed the burnt-out metal shell of the vehicles, with the blurred-out images of bodies and debris strewn across the road.
Police said the buses were hit with a glide bomb. 
The strikes come just a day after five children were among 22 killed when a Russian missile struck a five-storey apartment block in Pryluky, in the northern Chernigiv region.
"The Russians are deliberately targeting civilians," Donetsk Governor Vadym Filashkin said, accusing Moscow of flouting "every conceivable rule of warfare and norm of international humanitarian law".
fullText:
Ukraine on Thursday accused Russia of deliberately targeting civilians after 30 people were killed when two buses were blown up in the frontline city of Kramatorsk, in one of the deadliest single attacks for weeks.

Police said the buses were hit with a glide bomb.

The strikes come just a day after five children were among 22 killed when a Russian missile struck a five-storey apartment block in Pryluky, in the northern Chernigiv region.

"The Russians are deliberately targeting civilians," Donetsk Governor Vadym Filashkin said, accusing Moscow of flouting "every conceivable rule of warfare and norm of international humanitarian law".

Kramatorsk City Council called it "yet another horrific crime committed by the Russian army against the civilian population".

"Once again, the Russians have struck a location where there are absolutely no military targets," it added.

There has been mounting concern about the increase in civilian casualties in the conflict, as both sides step up long-range attacks beyond their borders.

Since Russia first invaded in 2022, Ukraine has accused its forces of deliberately attacking and killing civilians.

The United Nations has verified more than 17,000 civilian deaths throughout the war, but says the real number is considerably higher.

Last week, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin had sanctioned massive attacks on civilian areas.

The Kremlin has denied the claim.

Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, has come under increasing attack, including on Wednesday when Russia launched a barrage of powerful ballistic and cruise missiles, and fast-moving, jet-powered drones.

The city's mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said two people were found dead on Thursday after a fire at a four-storey building that was hit by a drone in the densely populated Solomyansky district.

Klitschko has said the attacks, which have hit key transport bridges in the city, as well as the rail network and energy grid, were "tearing Kyiv apart".

For the first few years of the war, Kyiv had been relatively spared from the devastation wrought on the frontline but should now be on a war footing, he argued.

Kramatorsk, which was home to some 150,000 people before the war, is one of the key cities that Russia has not yet captured in the eastern Donetsk region, which Moscow claims as its own.

It has been a logistics and supply hub for the Ukrainian military for much of the war and is part of the so-called "fortress belt" which troops are fighting to keep hold of.

Russian forces have edged close to the city's eastern fringes, which has prompted calls for the civilians who remain to relocate to safer regions of Ukraine.

Filashkin said Thursday's strike, which happened at 10:00 am (0700 GMT), represented a "sharp deterioration" in security and ordered the suspension of public transport in Kramatorsk and neighbouring Sloviansk.

"Under these circumstances, we cannot risk the lives of passengers and drivers," he said. "The safety of the residents of Kramatorsk and Sloviansk is now our top priority."

Ukraine last month launched a counter-offensive against Russian troops around Lyman -- to the north of Kramatorsk and Sloviansk -- claiming some success in regaining pockets of territory.

title: What vaccines doctors say you may need for respiratory virus season
description:
As the weather turns colder, it also means respiratory virus season is upon the United States.
In its annual outlook report, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it expects the 2026-27 respiratory virus season to have a similar number of peak hospitalizations from influenza, COVID-19 and RSV compared to last season.
Public health specialists told ABC News the best way for people to protect themselves against these viruses is to get vaccinated.
Expert tips for parents to prepare as flu season begins
Flu vaccine
The CDC currently recommends that people aged 6 months and older receive an annual flu vaccine.
The seasonal flu vaccine protects against three viruses predicted to circulate during flu season: Type A (H1N1) virus, Type A(H3N2) virus, and Type B/Victoria virus
There are several flu vaccines available this season, with recommendations varying by age and medical history.
fullText:
Doctors discuss COVID, flu and RSV vaccines recommended this year.

As the weather turns colder, it also means respiratory virus season is upon the United States.

In its annual outlook report, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it expects the 2026-27 respiratory virus season to have a similar number of peak hospitalizations from influenza, COVID-19 and RSV compared to last season.

Public health specialists told ABC News the best way for people to protect themselves against these viruses is to get vaccinated.

The CDC currently recommends that people aged 6 months and older receive an annual flu vaccine.

The seasonal flu vaccine protects against three viruses predicted to circulate during flu season: Type A (H1N1) virus, Type A(H3N2) virus, and Type B/Victoria virus

There are several flu vaccines available this season, with recommendations varying by age and medical history.

"Obviously, we target high-risk groups, so those would be older adults, so over the age of 50, people with chronic medical conditions, individuals who are immunocompromised, individuals that have obesity, or persons who are pregnant or wanting to get pregnant, and healthcare personnel," Dr. Michael Angarone, director of the Infectious Disease Fellowship Program at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine, told ABC News. "But I recommend every patient that I see should get vaccinated for influenza."

Standard-dose inactivated flu vaccines grown either in eggs or cell culture are available for anybody as young as 6 months old.

High-dose and adjuvanted flu vaccines, both of which are egg-based, are available for those aged 65 and older due to their higher risk of severe illness.

Anyone aged 9 and older can receive a recombinant flu vaccine, which is produced without eggs. For those between ages 2 and 49, who don't have certain medical conditions and aren't pregnant, a nasal spray flu vaccine is also available.

Additionally, in August, the Food and Drug Administration approved Moderna's mRNA seasonal flu vaccine to protect those aged 50 and older.

One dose is recommended for children between 6 months and 8 years old who have received two doses in past seasons and everyone aged 9 and older.

Some children under age 9 may require two doses based on prior vaccine history.

Public health specialists told ABC News they recommend that people receive flu vaccines by the end of October, but that people should get the vaccine even if later in the fall or winter as long as influenza viruses are circulating and unexpired vaccine is available.

Dr. Majd Alsoubani, infectious disease physician at Tufts Medical Center, said that one thing she often hears from patients is that every time they receive the vaccine, they get the flu -- which she says is a combination of misinformation and misunderstanding.

"All the injectable influenza vaccines, they don't have the live virus, it only contains parts of the virus, so it doesn't cause influenza," she told ABC News. "We know that the vaccine needs a couple of weeks just to create protection, so if they were exposed to influenza before the vaccine or right after, they actually might get the flu because the vaccine didn't have time to provide that protection."

People aged 18 and older are recommended to receive the COVID-19 vaccine, as are children ages 6 months to 17 years old at increased risk

Parents of all other children should speak to their pediatrician to discuss getting the vaccine.

The updated 2026-2027 COVID-19 vaccines target the XFG strain, a recombinant Omicron variant, meaning it formed through the combination of two Omicron subvariants.

Moderna's mRNA vaccine is approved for those 6 months through 64 years old with an underlying condition and for all adults aged 65 and older. Another Moderna mRNA vaccine that is a lower dosage is available for those ages 12 and older

Pfizer's mRNA vaccine is approved for those 5 years through 64 years old with an underlying condition and for all adults over age 65.

According to the CDC, underlying conditions placing people at risk for higher risk for severe COVID-19 include but are not limited to cancer, asthma, chronic lung disease, diabetes, heart conditions, mental health conditions and pregnancy.

Also available is a vaccine from Novavax, which is a protein-based vaccine, for those aged 12 and older.

Angarone said people can safely get the flu and COVID vaccine during the same visit if they are eligible.

"I recommend to my patients just get it at the same time, or if you don't want to get both at the same time, get [the COVID vaccine] a week apart from the flu vaccine," he said. "So, kind of around this time, October timeframe."

"The immunization recommendation kind of follows the people who are at risk of severe disease," Alsoubani said. "So the RSV vaccine currently is only one dose, so you're one and done. It's not an annual vaccine."

The CDC recommends RSV vaccines for all adults aged 75 and older and adults between ages 50 and 74 at increased risk for severe RSV.

It is also recommended for all pregnant people between 32 and 36 weeks' gestation.

For infants under 8 months who are in their first RSV season and whose mother did not receive a maternal RSV vaccine, two monoclonal antibody shots are available.

Monoclonal antibodies are proteins manufactured in a lab that mimic the antibodies the body naturally creates when fighting an infection.

A small group of young children between ages 8-19 months at increased risk for severe RSV may also be eligible.

title: Trump says former MLB pitcher Roger Clemens to be awarded Medal of Freedom
description:

Clemens introduced Trump at a rally in San Antonio on Wednesday, with Trump dropping the announcement as the former pitcher stood nearby. During the announcement, Trump said he had played golf with Clemens earlier this year, which prompted him to call MLB commissioner Rob Manfred about his Hall of Fame...
fullText:
Roger Clemens is not in the National Baseball Hall of Fame but he will receive the Presidential Medal of Freedom, President Donald Trump announced Wednesday.

Clemens introduced Trump at a rally in San Antonio on Wednesday, with Trump dropping the announcement as the former pitcher stood nearby. During the announcement, Trump said he had played golf with Clemens earlier this year, which prompted him to call MLB commissioner Rob Manfred about his Hall of Fame case:

"We had a great time, he's an amazing guy. I said, 'I'm going to call the commissioner of baseball.' It's a ridiculous thing that you're not in the Hall of Fame with that kind of record. He won seven Cy Youngs!"

It's worth noting the MLB commissioner has no power over who gets into the Hall of Fame. That is determined first by voters from the Baseball Writers Association of America (BBWAA), then a committee of voters determined by the Hall of Fame itself.

Trump did successfully intervene on the part of the late Pete Rose last year, pushing Manfred to remove the league's all-time hits leader from the ineligible list. Clemens is not on that list, nor will Rose reach the Hall of Fame without a successful vote.

Trump is correct that Clemens won seven Cy Young Awards, two more than any other pitcher in history. He also won two World Series championships, 11 All-Star selections, an AL MVP award, two 20-strikeout games and two triple crowns. It's one of the most impressive résumés in baseball history, but Clemens never received more than 65.2% of the BBWAA vote, or more than 25% of the vote in two go-arounds with the committee.

That would be due to rampant allegations of steroid use, which included dozens of mentions in the Mitchell Report based on testimony and evidence from his former trainer Brian McNamee, who said he injected Clemens with anabolic steroids and human growth hormone for years.

Clemens is generally accepted to have been a steroid user, but has always denied it. That was apparently enough for Trump, who chalked up Clemens' excellence in his 30s and 40s to natural athleticism:

"People talk drugs, he never admitted to anything. They have no information. They didn't find anything. It's not like, 'Oh jeez, load it up.' He never admitted to anything. He's just a physical monster, OK?"

Due to recent Hall of Fame rule changes, Clemens won't be considered for induction until at least 2031, and will be permanently ineligible if he again fails to receive at least five votes that year.

The Hall of Fame's character clause instructs voters to consider personal shortcomings with candidates, which has been the main justification for keeping steroid users out. With Clemens' case, it also comes up over allegations of a relationship with late country singer Mindy McCready.

In 2008, the New York Daily News reported that Clemens had been engaged in an affair with McCready since she was 15 years old. McCready confirmed she had a relationship with Clemens but denied it began when she was 15, while Clemens apologized for unspecified "mistakes in my personal life" but denied the claim that he had an improper relationship with a 15-year-old girl. McCready died by suicide in 2013 at the age of 37.

On Wednesday, Clemens said he was glad to receive the Medal of Freedom from Trump:

"I'm stunned, number one. Twenty-four years, y'all, this supersedes anything I've done in my playing career. To get it from this man, this president, there wouldn't be another president I'd want to get it from."

One awkward moment did come during the announcement, when Trump a) claimed Clemens was MLB's all-time leader in hit batters and b) said Clemens told him that resentment from hit batters was what sank his Hall of Fame eligibility:

"He was known for two things as a pitcher, power and accuracy. I said, 'Then Roger, how come you hit more batters than any other pitcher in history,' which is true. He hit more batters than any — and when he hit you, it hurt. When you have a ball going at 99 mph and it's aimed at your head — so Roger had some problems.

"He told me, part of the difficulty is the people on the board were people that he played against, so 'They all hate me.'"

Clemens is not MLB's all-time leader in HBPs, he ranks 15th in history with 159. If you narrow the group to only the live-ball era (since 1920), he's still only sixth.

Clemens himself disputed that claim while on stage:

"I don't think I lead Major League Baseball in hit batters, Mr. President."

As for the question of voters, the journalists that make up the BBWAA probably weren't annoyed about Clemens' propensity for hitting batters. As for the 16-person Contemporary Baseball Era committee that rejected Clemens in 2023 and 2026, we know who the voters were.

Former executives, veteran media members and baseball historians made up a majority of both committees. The players on the committees consisted of Chipper Jones, Greg Maddux, Jack Morris, Ryne Sandberg, Lee Smith, Frank Thomas, Alan Trammell, Fergie Jenkins, Jim Kaat, Juan Marichal, Tony Pérez, Ozzie Smith and Robin Yount. According to Stathead, none of Clemens' 159 HBPs were at the expense of any of those 13 players.

It remains to be seen when Clemens will receive the Medal of Freedom. Trump announced in Februrary that Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck would receive the Medal of Freedom for his heroics in Team USA's gold medal win at the Olympics.

Barring some sort of private ceremony, Hellebuyck has yet to receive the award.

title: Democrats and Republicans find rare common ground on kids' online safety
description:
